passages.mula:
दुर्गासप्तशती
गुप्तवत्यादिसप्तटीकासंवलिता
उपोद्धातः
श्रीगणेशाय नमः
वृषवाहनविघ्नेशौ हंसवाहां सरस्वतीम् ।
स्वेष्टं श्रीबटुकं नत्वा पितरं व्यङ्कटं ततः ॥१॥

श्रीगौतमकुलोत्पन्नो ज्योतिर्विद्व्यङ्कटात्मजः ।
हरिकृष्णः करोत्यत्र दुर्गोपासनसङ्ग्रहम् ॥२॥

अस्यामुपासनायां वै साधारणमपेक्षितम् ।
तत्सर्वं पूर्वमेवोक्तं विज्ञेयमिह चादरात् ॥३॥

पूर्वोक्तानां पदार्थानामत्र वक्ष्याम्यनुक्रमम् ।
लक्षणं गुरुशिष्याणां दीक्षाग्रहणनिर्णयः ॥४॥

पारायणविधानं चाभिषेकस्य विधानकम् ।
बीजानां लक्षणं चैव पुरश्चर्याविधिस्तथा ॥५॥

स्थानस्य निर्णयश्चैवासनस्य च विनिर्णयः ।
मुद्राणां लक्षणाध्यायो मालानिर्णय एच च ॥६॥

जपस्य लक्षणं चैव ह्यजपाजपलक्षणम् ।
तान्त्रिकं स्नानसन्ध्यादिनित्यकर्मनिरूपणम् ॥७॥

भूशुद्धिद्वारपूजादिदेहरक्षानिरूपणम्
भूतशुद्धिश्च प्राणानां प्रतिष्ठाविधिरेव च ॥८॥

न्यासानां निर्णयश्चैव मातृकान्यासनिर्णयः ।
अनेकविधन्यासानां सप्रमाणं निरूपणम् ॥९॥

अर्चनं द्विविधं चैव वामदक्षिणभेदतः ।
वामेन वा दक्षिणेन पूजनं तु यथारुचि ॥१०॥

पात्राणां लक्षणं चैव पात्रस्थापननिर्णयः ।
शुद्धिः पञ्चमकाराणां या वामे परिकीर्तिता ॥११॥

पात्राणां ग्रहणं चैव तिरस्करणिपूजनम् ।
अन्तर्यागविधानं च वैश्वदेवनिरूपणम् ॥१२॥

बहिर्यागविधानं च
सर्वयन्त्रप्रतिष्ठा
देवतापीठनिर्णयः ।
च सापि भेदद्वयात्मिका ॥१३॥

इष्टदेवस्थापनार्थं प्रथमं यन्त्रपूजनम् ।
वश्याद्यनेककार्येषु यानि यन्त्राणि सन्ति हि ॥१४॥

तेषां चैव प्रतिष्ठा च यन्त्रं सिद्धिकरं यतः-
अनेकविधपूजाया भेदलक्षणवर्णनम् ॥१५॥

शङ्खघण्टापूजनं च तन्माहात्म्यनिरूपणम् ।
उपासनाप्रभेदेन भस्मरुद्राक्षधारणम् ॥१६॥

गोपीचन्दनमाहात्म्यं तुलसीकाष्ठधारणम् ।
निर्णयश्चैव सम्प्रोक्तो ह्यावाहनविसर्जने ॥१७॥

आसनस्य च ध्यानस्य तथा पाद्यानिर्णयः ।
विधिराचमनीयस्य मधुपर्कस्य निर्णयः ॥१८॥

विधिः स्नानाभिषेकस्य जलाहरणनिर्णयः ।
वस्त्रस्य चोपवीतस्य तथालङ्करणस्य च ॥१९॥

गन्धाक्षतानां पुष्पाणां पत्राणां च विनिर्णयः ।
धूपदीपविधानं च नैवेद्यस्य विनिर्णयः ॥२०॥

फलताम्बूलयोश्चैव दक्षिणायाश्च निर्णयः ।
आरार्तिकमन्त्रपुष्पप्रदक्षिणविनिर्णयः ॥२१ ।।

प्रणामस्य प्रार्थनायास्तीर्थस्य च विनिर्णयः ।
अङ्गपूजाऽऽवर्णपूजा बलिदानादिनिर्णयः ॥२२॥

कुमारिकादिपूजायाः
स्तोत्रादिपठनं चैव
शक्तिपूजननिर्णयः ।
तीर्थग्रहणनिर्णयः ॥२३॥

होमस्य च विधानं वै कुण्डमण्डपलक्षणम् ।
तर्पणस्य मार्जनस्य द्विजसन्तर्पणस्य च ॥२४॥

गुप्तवत्युपोद्धातः । गुप्तवत्यादिसप्तटीकासंवलिता
विधानं च पृथक्प्रोक्तं निर्णयश्च पृथक्पृथक् ।
मन्त्रस्य शीघ्रसिद्धयर्थं विधिरुक्तो मया नृणाम् ॥२५॥

सर्वसिद्धिकरः साक्षान्मन्त्रसंस्कारपूर्वकः ।
मूलिकाग्रहणे मन्त्रा दिशां नियम एव च ॥२६॥

ऋतुमासर्क्षवाराणां तिथीनां नियमस्तथा ।
अङ्गुलीनिर्णय श्चैव वन्दाग्रहणनिर्णयः ॥२७॥

नपुंसकादिभेदाश्च मन्त्राणां ये प्रकीर्तिताः ।
पुरश्चरणतः पूर्वकृत्यं यच्चान्तिमे तथा ॥२९॥

तत्सर्वमपि ग्रन्थेऽस्मिन्पूर्वमेव प्रकीर्तितम् ।
आवर्णदेवतानां च यजनार्थ विशेषतः ॥३०॥

उद्धारश्चैव यन्त्राणां मन्त्रोद्धारस्तथैव च ।
सर्वेषां चैव देवानां गायत्रीमन्त्रसङ्ग्रहः ॥३१॥

चक्रपूजाविधिश्चैव काम्यपूजाविधिस्तथा ।
नैमित्तिकार्चनविधिर्विशेषेण निरूपितः ॥३२॥

गर्भाधानादिसंस्कारास्तान्त्रिकाश्च निरूपिताः ।
दीक्षितस्योपासकस्य ह्यन्त्येष्टिकर्मनिर्णयः ॥३३॥

कौलमार्गप्रकाशश्च कौलखण्डनमेव च ।
पूजापराधाः सम्प्रोक्ताः स्वस्तिकादिनिरूपणम् ॥३४॥

देवालयस्य मर्यादासेवनं च निरूपितम् ।
निर्णयश्चाधिकारश्च शब्दसृष्टिनिरूपणम् ॥३५॥

षडाम्नायस्य चोत्पत्तिः पवित्रदमनार्चनम् ।
मूर्तीनां लक्षणं चैव तपोमार्गनिदर्शनम्॥३६॥

जातिस्मरस्य चोपायाः प्रशंसा च निरूपिता ।
दुष्कर्मप्रायश्चित्तानि नित्यशिक्षानिरूपणम् ॥३७॥

शरीरस्य स्वरूपं च कामनाभेदनिर्णयः ।
पृथक्पृथक्तथाध्यायैः सर्वेषां निर्णयः स्फुटः ॥३८॥

परिभाषाभिधेऽध्याये केषाञ्चिन्निर्णयस्तथा ।
कृतस्तदनुरोधेन प्रयोगः सिद्धिदो नृणाम् ॥३९॥

अदृष्ट्वैव विधानं तु कृतश्चेन्नैव सेत्स्यति ।
एषां सर्वोपासनेषु ह्युपयोगो भवेत्किल ॥४०॥

तेषां सर्वपदार्थानां पूर्वमेव निरूपणम् ।
कृतं तस्माद्विशेषेण दृष्ट्वोपासनमारभेत् ॥४१॥

सर्वे शाक्ता द्विजाः प्रोक्ता न शैवा न च वैष्णवाः ।
आदिदेवीमुपासन्ते गायत्रीं वेदमातरम् ॥४२॥

तस्मादादौ प्रयत्नेन गायत्रीं प्रयुतं जपेत् ।
पटलं पद्धती वर्म तथा नामसहस्त्रकम् ॥४३॥

स्तोत्राणि चेति पञ्चाङ्गं देवतोपासने स्मृतम् ।
कवचं देवतागात्रं पटलं देवताशिरः ॥४४॥

पद्धतिर्देवहस्तौ तु मुखं साहस्त्रकं स्मृतम् ।
स्तोत्राणि देवतापादौ पञ्चाङ्गं पञ्चभिः स्मृतम् ॥४५॥

जपो होमस्तर्पणं च मार्जनं विप्रभोजनम् ।
आराधनं पञ्चविधं देवतानां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥४६॥

पञ्चाङ्गैः सहितं त्वेतद्दशानं कथ्यते बुधैः ।
हृदयं दीपदानं च स्तवराजादिकं तथा ॥४७॥

मालामन्त्रस्तथा कल्पः सर्वमेतद्ब्रवीम्यहम् ।
उपासना शराङ्गेषु या प्रोक्ता पद्धतिः पुरा ॥४८॥

इष्टदेवार्चनार्थं वै द्वितीयाङ्गं च तत्स्मृतम् ।
तस्यौपयोगिकं होतत्सर्वं पूर्वं मयोदितम् ॥४९॥

सविस्तरं च तदृष्ट्वा कार्या पद्धतिरुत्तमा ।
सनिर्णयां च सर्वत्र लिखामि यदि पद्धतिम् ॥५०॥

तदा ग्रन्थो महानेव भवेत्तस्माच्च पूर्वतः ।
लिखित्वा निर्णयः पश्चात्पटलादिकमत्र वै ॥५१॥

प्रवक्ष्यामि विशेषेण ग्रन्थानालोक्य यत्नतः ।
तस्माद्यत्नपरो भूयात्स्वस्य सिद्धयै न संशयः ॥५२॥

उपोद्धातप्रकरणं प्रथमं परिकीर्तितम् ।
दुर्गामाहात्म्यं पाद्योक्तं द्वितीयं च ततः परम् ॥५३॥

देवीरहस्यतन्त्रोक्तं दुर्गापञ्चाङ्गमीरितम् ।
अष्टमं च प्रकरणं दुर्गाभुवनवर्णनम् ॥५४॥

पञ्चरत्नेश्वरीविद्या दुर्गास्तोत्रं ततः परम् ।
ब्रह्मवैवर्तसम्प्रोक्तं दुर्गाकवचमुत्तमम् ॥५५॥

अष्टोत्तरशतं नामस्तोत्रं तन्त्रोक्तमेव च ।
रुद्रचण्डीप्रकरणं त्रयोदशममीरितम् ॥५६॥

रुद्रयामलतन्त्रोक्तं सूक्तत्रयमतः परम् ।
मालामन्त्रश्चण्डिकायाः शूलिनीमन्त्र एव च ॥५७॥

वनदुर्गोपनिषदं दुर्गोपनिषदं तथा ।
देवीमहिम्नस्तोत्रं च दुर्गास्तवमतः परम् ॥५८॥

एकविंशे प्रकरणे दुर्गाकल्पः प्रकीर्तितः ।
मार्कण्डेयपुराणोक्तं सूक्तत्रयमुदीरितम् ॥५९॥

चण्डिकाहृदयं चैव चण्डिकास्तोत्रमेव च ।
लघुदुर्गासप्तशतीस्तोत्रं कवचमेव च ॥६०॥

कुञ्जिकातन्त्रसम्प्रोक्तं दुर्गास्तोत्रं ततः परम् ।
गुरुकीलकसंज्ञं वै पटलं परिकीर्तितम् ॥६१॥

तथा मन्त्रविभागश्च सम्प्रोक्तोऽष्टप्रभेदतः ।
दुर्गायाः पटलं चैव नित्यदुर्गाविधानकम् ॥६२॥

नवचण्डीविधानं च नवरात्रिविधानकम् ।
शतचण्डीविधानं च सहस्रायुतलक्षकम् ॥६३॥

दुर्गामखप्रयोगश्च दीपदानविधिस्ततः ।
नित्यार्चनप्रयोगश्च तथा नैमित्तिकार्चनम् ॥६४॥

दुर्गादमनपूजा च पवित्रारोपणं तथा ।
एकचत्वारिंशके तु जयदुर्गाविधानकम् ॥६५ ॥

दुर्गाषोडशनामाख्यं स्तोत्रं सार्थं ततः परम् ।
श्रीजामदग्न्यसम्प्रोक्तं दुर्गास्तोत्रं सविस्तरम् ॥६६॥

तथा गणेशखण्डोक्तं दुर्गाकवचमेव च ।
दकारपूर्वकं स्तोत्रं दुर्गानामसहस्रकम् ॥६७॥

नामावली च तस्यैव तथा चाष्टोत्तरस्य च ।
शतस्य नामावलिका दुर्गानीराजनं ततः ॥६८ ॥

श्रीदुर्गाब्रह्मकवचमर्गलाकीलकं तथा ।
न्यासाश्च रात्रिसूक्तं च दुर्गासप्तशती तथा ॥६९॥

देवीसूक्तं रहस्यानि दुर्गासंहार एव च ।
देवीगीता च सम्प्रोक्ता साक्षान्निर्वाणदायिनी ॥७०॥

एतत्सर्वं मया पूर्वं हरिकृष्णेन धीमता ।
ज्योतिषार्णवमध्यस्थे स्कन्थे वै धर्मसंज्ञके ॥७१॥

उपासनाख्ये स्तबके विस्तरेण निरूपितम् ।
अतः परं चार्थबोधज्ञानार्थमिदमुच्यते ॥७२॥

गुप्तवतीटीकास्थः सप्तशत्युपोद्यातः
श्रीगणेशाय नमः

तां धेनुं समुपह्वयामि सुदुधामित्यृग्गतं शङ्करा-
चार्यं शिष्यचतुष्टयेन सहितं वन्दे गुरूणां गुरुम् ॥१॥

विधिविष्णुमुखामरोदयस्थितिनाशेषु शिवोऽप्यनीश्वरः ।
जगदम्ब तव त्वयं क्रमः क्षणमुद्दालकपुष्पभञ्जिका ॥२॥

कवचार्गले च कीलकमादौ मध्ये त्रयोदशाध्यायी ।
अन्ते प्राधानिकवैकृतिके मूर्तित्रयं रहस्यानाम् ॥३॥

इति मार्कण्डेयपुराणाध्यायेषूनविंशतौ गुप्तान् ।
अर्थान् प्रकटीकुरुते भास्कररायोऽग्निचित् कतिचित् ॥४॥

सप्तशती लुप्तसृतीराप्तवती सत्यतीव तप्तवती ।
मम तु मतीरचितवती गुप्तवती नाम बिभ्रतीं विवृतिम् ॥५॥

काव्यव्याकृतितार्किकौपनिषदेष्वेकैकविद्भिः कृता-
ष्टीकाः सन्ति चतुर्विधा अपि चमत्कारावहास्तद्विदाम् ।
ताश्चण्डीजपहोमतर्पणमुखानुष्ठानमात्रोपयो
ग्यर्थज्ञानमभीप्सतां न विदुषां चित्ते चमत्कुर्वते ॥६॥

एतद्गन्धरसास्वादसामर्थ्य विदुषां यदि ।
किमिति प्रार्थनीयास्ते न चेत् प्रार्थनयापि किम् ॥७॥

कैः पुष्पैरक्षतान् दत्त्वा भृङ्गा भुवि निमन्त्रिताः ।
केन वा चम्पकेनार्धचन्द्रं दत्त्वा निराकृताः ॥८॥

यत् सप्तशत्यायुषि गुप्तवत्यामपेक्षणीयं तदवेक्षणीयम् ।
चण्डीसपक्रमकल्पवल्ल्यां यत्तत्र गुप्तं तदिहास्ति क्लृप्तम् ॥९॥

तत्रादौ वक्ष्यमाणार्थानुक्रमणीश्लोकाश्चतुर्दश लिख्यन्ते-
मङ्गलाचरणं ग्रन्थप्रतिपाद्यार्थसङ्ग्रहः ।
ततश्चण्डीतिशब्दस्य तदर्थस्य च निर्णयः ॥१॥

तन्मन्त्रस्य नवार्णस्योद्धारस्तस्यार्थवर्णनम् ।
चण्डीस्तवेऽपि हल्लेखा वाग्भवं चेतनी रमा ॥२॥

कामः कामकला विघ्नो वाराही नारसिंहिकाः ।
परा प्रासादतद्योगसर्वमङ्गलकालिकाः ॥३॥

नवार्णश्चेति सर्वेषां मन्त्रोद्धारप्रवेशनम् ।
सङ्क्षेपेण नवार्णस्य साधनक्रमवर्णनम् ॥४॥

अङ्गाङ्गी भावनिष्कर्षचण्डीस्तवनवार्णयोः
ततः सप्तशतीशब्दस्तदर्थस्तत्प्रशंसनम् ॥५॥

शापोद्धारोत्कीर्तने च तत्स्तोत्रपठनक्रमः ।
तत्पुरश्चरणं काम्यप्रयोगे बलिनिर्णयः ॥६॥

आवृत्तौ पाठवैचित्र्यमृत्विजान्दक्षिणाक्रमः ।
कवचस्यार्गलायाश्च कीलकस्यार्थवर्णनम्॥७॥

ततो रहस्यतन्त्रस्थगुरुकीलकलेखनम् ।
तदर्थवर्णनं कात्यायनीतन्त्रस्य मुख्यता ॥८॥

तत्राद्यपटलव्याख्या परोक्ताभासखण्डनम् ।
ततस्तत्सङ्ग्रहशतश्लोक्या अंशेन लेखनम् ॥९॥

ด
स्तोत्राद्यचरितव्याख्या द्वितीयपटलस्य च ।
तत्सङ्ग्रहांशो व्याख्यानं मध्यमेऽथ चरित्रके ॥१०॥

तृतीयपटलव्याख्या ततस्तत्सङ्ग्रहांशकः ।
तृतीयचरितेऽध्यायषट्कमन्त्रार्थवर्णनम् ॥११॥

चतुर्थपटलव्याख्या ततस्तत्सङ्ग्रहांशकः ।
एकादशादित्रितयमन्त्राध्यायार्थवर्णनम् ॥१२॥
ततस्तन्त्रान्तरप्रोक्तसङ्ग्रहांशसमापनम् ॥१३॥

प्राधानिकरहस्यस्य व्याख्या वैकृतिकस्य च ।
ततो मूर्तिरहस्यस्येत्यनुक्रमणिका मता ॥१४॥

चण्डीनाम परब्रह्मणः पट्टमहिषी देवता । चण्डभानुश्चण्डवाद
वियत्तानवच्छिन्नाऽसाधारणगुणशालिपरत्वेन चण्डपदस्य प्रयोगदर्शनात्,
देशकालवस्तुकृतत्रैविध्येन तादृशपरिच्छेदत्रितयराहित्यस्य परब्रह्मैकलिङ्गत्वात्,
चडि कोप इति धातोनिष्पत्तिस्तदापि-
'कस्य बिभ्यति देवाश्च जातरोषस्य संयुगे । इत्यादिना,
यद्यपि
तत्र
'प्रसादो निष्फलो यस्य कोपोऽपि च निरर्थकः ।
न तं भर्तारमिच्छन्ति षण्ढं पतिमिव 'स्त्रियः' ॥
इत्यादा-
इयत्तायाश्च
इत्यादिना च महाभयजनकत्वेनैव कोपस्य साफल्योक्तेस्तादृश एव कोपे
खड्गं चक्रगदेषुचापपरिघान् शूलं भुशुण्डीं शिरः

शूलं पाशसुदर्शने च दधतीं हस्तैः प्रवालप्रभा
सेवे सौरिभमर्दिनीमिह महालक्ष्मी सरोजस्थिताम् ॥२॥

घण्टां शूलहलानि शङ्खमुसले चक्रं धनुः सायकान्
हस्ताब्जैर्दधतीं घनान्तविलसच्छीतांशुतुल्यप्रभाम् ।
गौरीदेहसमुद्भवां त्रिजगतामाधारभूत महा-
पूर्वामत्र सरस्वतीमनुभजे शुम्भादिदैत्यार्दिनीम् ॥३॥

इति ध्यात्वा मनसाऽन्तर्यागं कृत्वा बर्हिर्यागमपि यन्त्रे कुर्यात्।
यन्त्रं यथा-
'लिखेदष्टदलं पयं कुङ्कमागरुचन्दनैः ।
पद्ममध्ये लिखेच्चक्रं षट्कोणं चण्डिकामयम् ॥
षट्कोणचक्रमध्यस्थमाद्यं बीजत्रयं न्यसेत्।
पूर्वादिकोणषट्के तु बीजान्यन्यानि विन्यसेत् ॥

'जपेट् बिल्वं समाश्रित्य मासमेकं तु यो नरः ।
हुत्वा बिल्वदलैर्मासं मधुरत्रययोगतः ॥
हुत्वा दशांशतो वापि कमलैः क्षीरसंयुतैः ।
धनदेन समां लक्ष्मीं प्राप्नुयादुत्तमां ध्रुवम् ॥ इति ॥
अथ प्रयोगान्तराणि कात्यायनीतन्त्रोक्तानि। प्रतिश्लोकमाद्यन्तयोः मन्त्र
जपेन्मन्त्रसिद्धिः । सप्रणवमनुलोमव्याहृतित्रयमादौ अन्ते तु विलोमं तदित्येव
प्रतिश्लोकं कृत्वा शतावृत्तिपाठे अतिशीघ्रं सिद्धिः । प्रतिश्लोकमादौ जातवेदस इति
ऋचं पठेत्सर्वकामसिद्धिः ।
अपमृत्युवारणायादावन्ते शतं त्र्यम्बकमन्त्रं जपेत्। प्रतिश्लोकं तन्मन्त्रजप
इति वा। प्रतिश्लोकं शरणागतेति श्लोकं पठेत्सर्वकार्यसिद्धिः । प्रतिश्लोकं करोतु

यगुह्यं परमं लोके सर्वरक्षाकरं नृणाम्।
यन्न कस्यचिदाख्यातं तन्मे बूहि पितामह ॥१॥

ॐ सत्सम्प्रदायप्रथनाय तिष्ये शिष्यैश्चतुर्भिः सह योऽवतीर्णः ।
उक्तो बृहत्सङ्गमतन्त्रराजे श्रीशङ्कराचार्यगुरुं तमीडे ॥१॥

संसार में अत्यन्त गोपनीय मनुष्यों की सभी प्रकार से रक्षा करने वाला तथा
जो आजतक आपने किसी के लिए न कहा हो, वह (साधन) मुझसे कहें॥१॥
passages.primaryEn: The book opens with a disciple's humble question. In simple words: O Master, please teach me that most secret practice which protects people in every way — the one you have never told anyone until today. (Verse 1, Hindi.) This single prayer opens the entire Kavaca (armour) teaching that follows.

passages.mula:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अस्ति गुह्यतमं विप्र सर्वभूतोपकारम् ।
देव्यास्तु कवचं पुण्यं तच्छृणुष्व महामुने ॥२॥
passages.primaryEn: Brahmā answers: O learned one, there is indeed a most secret and holy armour of the Goddess that helps all beings — listen to it, O great sage. (Verse 2.) Combined with the commentary: whatever you asked for, O Brāhmaṇa, such a holy armour of the Goddess alone exists — keep it like a buried treasure. 'Great sage' is used because this teaching works for the welfare of all creatures.

passages.mula:
स्थापितमस्ति तन्महामुने शृणुष्व। सर्वभूतोपकारार्थं प्रवृत्तत्वान्महामने इति
सम्बोधनम् ॥२॥
passages.primaryEn: Brahmā said: the armour that helps all beings, most secret and holy, is the Goddess's Kavaca itself — listen, O great sage. (Verse 2, Hindi.) In simple words the teacher confirms: yes, such a protective shield exists, it belongs to the Goddess alone, and hearing it with respect is itself a blessing.

passages.mula:
प्रथमं शैलपुत्रीति द्वितीयं ब्रह्मचारिणी
तृतीयं चन्द्रघण्टेति कूष्माण्डेति चतुर्थकम् ॥३॥
passages.primaryEn: First (Her name is) Śailaputrī, second Brahmacāriṇī, third Candraghaṇṭā, and fourth Kūṣmāṇḍā. (Verse 3.) Combined with the commentaries: because the Goddess is to be meditated as nine-formed, Her nine names are listed — and once you know a name, you easily recognise whom it points to. Śailaputrī: though supreme over all, out of love She accepted becoming the lowly mountain-king's daughter when He prayed with hard penance — what words can describe such love for devotees! Brahmacāriṇī: She whose nature is to carry seekers to Brahman, the blissful reality — giver of Brahmanhood. Candraghaṇṭā: She whose hand-bell shines spotless like the moon — the Goddess who makes hearts bloom with joy, more lovely even than the moon.

passages.mula:
शैलपुत्री, दूसरी का नाम ब्रह्मचारिणी, तीसरी का नाम चन्द्रघण्टा तथा चौथी
का नाम कुष्माण्डा है।।३।।
passages.primaryEn: The first form is named Śailaputrī, the second Brahmacāriṇī, the third Candraghaṇṭā and the fourth Kuṣmāṇḍā. (Verse 3, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee counts the Mother's first four of nine forms on the fingers: the mountain's daughter, the maiden of Brahman, the moon-belled one, and the cosmic-egg warmer.

passages.mula:
पञ्चमं स्कन्दमातेति षष्ठं कात्यायनीति च ।
सप्तमं कालरात्रीति महागौरीति चाष्टमम् ॥४॥
passages.primaryEn: Fifth is called Skandamātā, sixth Kātyāyanī, seventh Kālarātrī, and eighth Mahāgaurī. (Verse 4.) Combined with the commentaries: Skandamātā — mother of Skanda (the scriptures say even wise men long to be born from such a womb, so pure is She). Kātyāyanī — She who appeared in sage Kātyāyana's hermitage for the gods' mission and was accepted as his daughter; ever-maiden, under no husband, fully free. Kālarātrī — the night that swallows even Time, the killer of all, since at the world's end even Time itself dies. Mahāgaurī — the greatly self-respecting one who, when called 'dark' by Śiva in jest, won a fair golden color by penance, as the Kālī Purāṇa tells clearly.

passages.mula:
नवमं सिद्धिदा प्रोक्तां नवदुर्गाः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
उक्तान्येतानि नामानि ब्रह्मणैव महात्मना ॥५॥
passages.primaryEn: The ninth is famed as the giver of occult powers (Siddhidā) — thus the Nine Durgās are declared; and these names were spoken by the great-souled Brahmā himself. (Verse 5.) Combined with the commentary: 'giver of powers' means giver of final freedom; these nine are not nine different goddesses but nine faces of the one Durgā, like a yogi's many body-forms — and I (Brahmā) have declared exactly those forms the scriptures ask us to meditate.

passages.mula:
देव्यास्तु कवचमित्येकवचनं सङ्गच्छते। नाम्नां स्वकल्पितत्वशङ्काव्युदासार्थमाह।
उक्तान्येतानीति। महात्मना सर्वज्ञेन ब्रह्मणैव वेदेनैवैतान्युक्तानीत्यर्थः।।५॥
passages.primaryEn: That is why the armour is spoken of in the singular — 'the Kavaca of the Goddess'. And lest anyone doubt these names are man-made, the verse adds: the all-knowing great-souled Brahmā — the Veda itself — spoke all these names. (Verse 5, explanation.) Combined with the notes: one book reads 'Siddhidātrī' here; the Hindi prayer repeats — the ninth face is Siddhidātrī, these are the Nine Durgās, and every name comes from all-knowing Brahmā, the Veda-Lord Himself.

passages.mula:
अग्निना दह्यमानस्तु शत्रुमध्ये गतो रणे ।
विषमे दुर्गमे चैव भर्याताः शरणं गताः ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: One burning in fire, fallen among enemies in battle, or terrified in rough and impassable places, if they take shelter (of Her) — (verses 6–7 begin). In simple words: whoever runs to the Mother while burning, trapped among enemies in war, or trembling in a dangerous lonely spot — listen to what happens to them next.

passages.mula:
न तेषां जायते किञ्चिदशुभं रणसङ्कटे ।
नापदं तस्य पश्यामि शोकदुःखभयं न हि ॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: No evil befalls them even in the crisis of battle; I see for them no danger, no grief, no sorrow, no fear. (Verses 6–7.) Combined with the commentaries: whoever chants the nine names (supply this while reading), and even the many others who merely shelter behind that one chanter — for all of them, and for him, all harm is removed. That is the joint meaning of both verses: those burning, those war-trapped, those terror-struck in dreadful places — once sheltered, no mishap in battle, and as for sorrow, pain and fear, the seer declares: I simply do not see any for them.

passages.mula:
तेषां तस्य च भक्तिरहितेन स्मरणमात्रेणापि तज्जन्यं भयादिकं न
भवतीत्याह । न तेषामिति॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: Even by mere remembrance without deep devotion, the fear born of such dangers simply does not arise — so the verse declares. (Explanation of verse 7.) In simple words: you don't even need perfect devotion; just remembering Her once is enough to keep fear away.

passages.mula:
होता है। उस व्यक्ति की किसी भी प्रकार की- शोक, दुःख एवं भय आदि
आपत्ति को मैं नहीं देख रहा हूँ।।६॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: Whoever is burning in fire, fallen among enemies in battle, or terrified in rough impassable places and reaches the shelter of Goddess Durgā — no evil touches them even in war's crisis. I see no calamity of any kind for such a person — no grief, no sorrow, no fear. (Verses 6–7, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats the promise slowly: fire, enemies, wilderness — take shelter once, and no harm, no sorrow, no fear can touch you.

passages.mula:
यैस्तु भक्तत्या स्मृता नूनं तेषामृद्धिः प्रजायते ।
प्रेतसंस्था तु चामुण्डा वाराही महिषासना ॥८॥
passages.primaryEn: But by those by whom (She) is remembered with devotion — theirs, surely, is prosperity. (Then) Cāmuṇḍā seated on a corpse, Vārāhī riding a buffalo. (Verse 8.) In simple words: the frightened get protection (verses 6–7); but those who remember Her with love get more — certain growth and glory. Then the hymn begins describing the Seven Mothers who guard the chanter.

passages.mula:
ऐन्द्री गजसमारूढा वैष्णवी गरुडासना ।
माहेश्वरी वृषारूढा कौमारी शिखिवाहना ॥९॥
passages.primaryEn: Aindrī mounted on an elephant, Vaiṣṇavī seated on Garuḍa; Māheśvarī riding a bull, Kaumārī with the peacock as vehicle. (Verse 9.) In simple words: Indra's power rides the elephant, Viṣṇu's power rides Garuḍa, Śiva's power rides the bull, Kumāra's power rides the peacock — the Mother's seven warrior faces, each on Her own mount.

passages.mula:
सिद्धिरिति पाठान्तरम्। सिद्धिर्ज्ञानम्। आर्तानिष्टनिरासानुगुण एव सप्तमातृणां
सार्वदिक उद्योग इत्याह। प्रेतसंस्थेत्यादिना ।।८॥९॥
passages.primaryEn: Having told the fruit of devotion in distress, now the fruit of the seeker's devotion: 'by whomsoever' — theirs is attainment. One reading says 'perfection' (siddhi) instead of 'prosperity' — and perfection means true knowledge. Then, ever-active for removing devotees' troubles, come the Seven Mothers, described across two verses (8–9). Combined with the notes: remembrance with love surely brings the earlier fruit — and what to say of it, it brings the four goals of life (duty, wealth, desire, freedom) too. One book reads 'growth' (vṛddhi) for 'prosperity'. The Goddess's overflowing motherly love is shown here only to grow our devotion.

passages.mula:
देवी का आसन गरुड़ है। माहेश्वरी वृषभ पर आरूढ होती हैं। कौमारी का वाहन
मयूर है।८॥९॥
passages.primaryEn: The mount of the Goddess is Garuḍa (Vaiṣṇavī); Māheśvarī rides the bull; Kaumārī's vehicle is the peacock. (Verses 8–9, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee pictures each Mother on Her own mount — corpse, buffalo, elephant, Garuḍa, bull, peacock — seven guardians shining together.

passages.mula:
विशेष- 'वैस्तु भक्त्या स्मृता नूनम्' इसके बाद कुछ प्रतियों में 'ये
त्वां स्मरन्ति देवेशि रक्षसे तान्न संशयः' ऐसा पाठ मिलता है।
नीलकण्ठ या भास्करराय आदि प्राचीन व्याख्याकारों ने इसे कवच में नहीं
माना है। इसी प्रकार नवें श्लोक के पश्चात्-
लक्ष्मीः प‌द्मासना देवी पद्महस्ता हरिप्रिया ।
श्वेतरूपधरा देवी ईश्वरी वृषवाहना ।
नारसिंही महावीर्या शिवदूती महाबला ।
इन श्लोकों का पाठ भी कुछ प्रतियों में प्राप्त होता है, जो प्राचीन
टीकाकारों द्वारा अव्याख्यात होने के कारण कवच में सम्मिलित नहीं है।
कवच के दशवें श्लोक के पूर्वार्ध के पश्चात् कुछ प्रतियों में- 'इत्येता
मातरः सर्वाः सर्वयोगसमन्विताः' ऐसा पाठ भी मिलता है, जिसे प्राचीन
passages.primaryEn: A caution about extra verses: after 'remembered with devotion' some books add 'those who remember You, O Lord of gods, You protect them, no doubt' — but ancient explainers like Nīlakaṇṭha and Bhāskararāya never accepted it in the Kavaca. Likewise after verse 9 some copies carry three verses on Lakṣmī, the white-formed Goddess, Nārasiṃhī and Śivadūtī — also unexplained by old commentators, so left out. And before verse 10's second half some read 'all these Mothers, rich in all yogas' — also not accepted by the ancients. (For detail the edition points to Paṇḍit Rājakiśoramaṇi Tripathī's Devī-Māhātmya study.) In simple words: only the verses the old masters explain belong to the real Kavaca; later additions, however sweet, are kept out.

passages.mula:
ब्राह्मी हंससमारूढा सर्वाभरणभूषिता ।
नानाभरणशोभाढ्या नानारत्नोपशोभिताः ॥१०॥
passages.primaryEn: Brāhmī seated on a swan, adorned with every ornament; shining with many jewels and many decorations. (Verse 10.) In simple words: Brahmā's power glides on a swan, dressed in all ornaments — the first of the Mothers in their full glory.

passages.mula:
दृश्यन्ते रथमारूढा देव्यः क्रोधसमाकुलाः ।
शवं चक्रं गदां शक्तिं हलं च मुसलायुधम् ॥११॥
passages.primaryEn: Goddesses are seen mounted on chariots, blazing with anger — conch, discus, mace, spear, plough and club as weapons. (Verse 11.) In simple words: beyond the seven, more warrior goddesses roll in on chariots, furious to protect, holding conch and discus and mace.

passages.mula:
खेटकं तोमरं चैव परशुं पाशमेव च ।
कुन्तायुधं त्रिशूलं च शायुधमनुत्तमम् ॥१२॥
passages.primaryEn: Shield and javelin too, axe and noose; the spear-weapon and the trident, and the supreme wonderful bow. (Verse 12.) In simple words the armoury list continues — shield, spear, axe, noose, lance, trident and the finest of bows — heaven's whole arsenal in the Mothers' hands.

passages.mula:
दैत्यानां देहनाशाय भक्तानामभयाय च ।
धारयन्त्यायुधानीत्थं देवानां च हिताय वै ॥१३॥
passages.primaryEn: To destroy the demons' bodies, to grant fearlessness to devotees, and for the welfare of the gods — thus they hold these weapons. (Verse 13.) Combined with the commentaries: other goddesses beyond the seven, also mounted on chariots in anger for devotees' protection, are seen — by gods and men. Their weapons are then listed (verses 10–12). And why do the Seven Mothers hold conch, discus and the rest? For three reasons together: to finish demons' bodies, to give devotees fearlessness, and to serve the gods. The feeling behind it: even unasked, these great goddesses rush to protect the world purely out of motherly love — so why should unlucky little me not beg them for my own protection, like a child asking its mother?

passages.mula:
महाबले महोत्साहे महाभयविनाशिनि ।
त्राहि मां देवि दुःप्रेक्ष्ये शत्रूणां भयवर्धिनी ॥१४॥
passages.primaryEn: O mighty, O greatly eager, O destroyer of great fear — protect me, O Goddess hard to behold, O increaser of the foes' terror! (Verse 14.) Combined with the commentaries: from here the devotee himself starts praying. Read this prayer-mantra first, then the Kavaca — that is the rule. 'Great strength' is Her power of illusion itself; 'great eagerness' is Her zeal to protect the world; 'destroyer of great fear' destroys death-like terror by giving wisdom; 'hard to behold' — Her form stands beyond sight, as the scripture says; and the 'foes' are lust, anger and their kin.

passages.mula:
करने वाली! कठिनता से देखे जाने वाली! शत्रुओं के भय को बढ़ाने वाली !
देवी ! मेरी रक्षा करो।।१४॥
passages.primaryEn: O greatly strong! O greatly eager! O destroyer of great fears! O hard to behold! O increaser of the foes' terror! O Goddess, protect me. (Verse 14, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee cries out Her titles one by one — strength, zeal, fear-killer, unseeable, terror to enemies — and begs: protect me.

passages.mula:
प्राच्यां रक्षतु मामैन्द्री आग्नेय्यामग्निदेवता ।
दक्षिणे रक्ष वाराहि नैऋत्यां खड्गधारिणी ॥१५॥
passages.primaryEn: In the east may Aindrī protect me; in the south-east the fire-goddess. In the south, protect, O Vārāhī; in the south-west, O sword-bearer. (Verse 15.) Combined with the commentaries: grammar first — where the goddess-name ends in the nominative ('may Aindrī protect'), the verb runs in third person; where it ends in address ('protect, O Vārāhī'), it runs in second person — each verb simply carries forward to its own line. Meaning: Aindrī, Indra's power standing in the east, protect me (or: protect me standing in the east — both read the same, since power and its holder are one). Vārāhī is Yama's power (Varāha = Yama in ancient usage) — O Vārāhī, standing in the south, protect me. The sword-bearer is Nirṛti's power in the south-west. One book reads 'hard to behold' (duṣprekṣye) in verse 14.

passages.mula:
प्रतीच्यां वारुणी रक्षेद्वायव्यां मृगवाहिनी ।
रक्षेदुदीच्या कौमारी ईशान्यां शूलधारिणी ॥१६॥
passages.primaryEn: In the west may Vāruṇī protect; in the north-west, She who rides a deer. In the north may Kaumārī protect; in the north-east, She who holds a spear. (Verse 16.) Combined with the commentary: the deer-rider is the wind-god's power (the wind rides a deer); Kaumārī here is Kubera's power (Kumāra = Kubera, whose pride is ugly — the joke hidden in the name), guarding the north though her full station comes later — and one goddess guarding two stations is no fault at all; or She is the Kaumārī among the Seven Mothers, and the spear-holder is Īśāna's power.

passages.mula:
वक्ष्यमाणमस्ति तथाप्येकस्या एव स्थानद्वयरक्षकत्वे बाधकाभावः। सप्तमात्रन्तर्गता
वा कौमारी शूलधारिणी। ईशानशक्तिरित्यर्थः ।।१६॥
passages.primaryEn: The Hindi of the same prayer: the deer-rider's openly stated station comes ahead, yet one goddess guarding two stations is no contradiction — whether as Kubera's power or as the Kaumārī of the Seven Mothers, and the spear-holder as Īśāna's power. (Verse 16, explanation.) In simple words: don't worry if one Mother guards two directions — a mother can watch two children at once.

passages.mula:
करने वाली देवी मेरी रक्षा करे। उत्तर दिशा में कौमारी तथा ईशान कोण में
शूलधारिणी देवी रक्षा करे ।।१६॥
passages.primaryEn: In the west may Vāruṇī, in the north-west the deer-riding Goddess protect me. In the north Kaumārī and in the north-east the spear-holding Goddess protect me. (Verse 16, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee turns around the compass — west, north-west, north, north-east — posting a Mother at every corner.

passages.mula:
ऊर्ध्वं ब्रह्माणि मे रक्षेदधस्ताद्वैष्णवी तथा ।
एवं दशदिशो रक्षेच्चामुण्डा शववाहना ॥१७॥
passages.primaryEn: Above may Brāhmī protect me, and below likewise Vaiṣṇavī. Thus in all ten directions may Cāmuṇḍā, who rides a corpse, protect. (Verse 17.) Combined with the commentary: 'O Brāhmī' — You who bring Brahmā (fetch and revive all beings), standing above, protect me (or: protect my upper part — same sense). So too below. Then 'thus' — in the manner of the ten direction-guardians — may Cāmuṇḍā protect my ten directions, my kin-directions; for Cāmuṇḍā stationed in all ten directions protects me — that is the settled meaning, since merely guarding empty directions would serve no purpose.

passages.mula:
भाग में वैष्णवी देवी मेरी रक्षा करें। इसी प्रकार शव को अपना वाहन बनाने
वाली चामुण्डा देवी दशों दिशाओं में मेरी रक्षा करें ।। १७।।
passages.primaryEn: O Brāhmī, protect me in the upper region, and may Vaiṣṇavī protect me below. Likewise may Cāmuṇḍā, who makes a corpse Her vehicle, protect me in all ten directions. (Verse 17, Hindi.) In simple words: sky above, earth below, and all ten sides around — every direction gets its guarding Mother, with corpse-riding Cāmuṇḍā watching the whole circle.

passages.mula:
जया मे चाग्रतः स्था विजया स्थातुं पृष्ठतः ।
अजिता वामपार्श्वे तु दक्षिणे चापराजिता ॥१८॥
passages.primaryEn: May Jayā stand before me, Vijayā behind; Ajitā to my left, and Aparājitā to my right. (Verse 18.) Combined with the commentaries: 'let her stand' in the ancient style; Jayā is a power-goddess — may she stand firm, all for my protection.

passages.mula:
शिखामुद्योतिनी रक्षेदुमा मूनि व्यवस्थिता ।
मालाधरी ललाटे च भ्रुवौ रक्षेद्यशस्विनी ॥१९॥
passages.primaryEn: May Udyotinī guard (my) hair-top, Umā stationed on the crown; Mālādhārī on the forehead, and Yaśasvinī guard the brows. (Verse 19.) Combined with the commentaries: read every limb the same way — the goddess named Udyotinī, stationed at my hair-top, guards my hair-top; and so for each. Wherever the verse names only the station (first line) supply 'guarding', and wherever only guarding (second line) supply 'stationed' — apply this joining rule everywhere through the whole body-list.

passages.mula:
नोच्यते तदन्यतरत्तत्राध्याहार्यम्। यथाऽत्रैव प्रथमचरणेऽवस्थापनस्य द्वितीयचरणे
रक्षणस्याध्याहारः । एवं सर्वत्र।। १९॥
passages.primaryEn: Whatever of the two patterns is unsaid in either place, supply the other one there. (Explanation of the joining rule, verse 19.) In simple words the commentators give the key to the whole list: each line either says where She stands or what She guards — you silently add the missing half, and the meaning completes itself, everywhere alike.

passages.mula:
त्रिनेत्रा च भ्रुवोर्मध्ये यमघण्टा च नासिके ।
शङ्खिनी चक्षुषोर्मध्ये श्रोत्रयो रिवासिनी ॥२०॥
passages.primaryEn: Trinetrā between the brows, and Yamaghaṇṭā at the nose; Śaṅkhinī between the eyes, Dvāravāsinī at the ears. (Verse 20.) In simple words the guard-posting moves down the face: the three-eyed one between the brows, the death-bell at the nose, the conch-lady between the eyes, the door-keeper at the ears.

passages.mula:
कपोलौ कालिका रक्षेत्कर्णमूले तु शङ्करी ।
नासिकायां सुगन्धा च उत्तरोष्ठे च चर्चिका ॥२१॥
passages.primaryEn: May Kālikā guard the cheeks, Śaṅkarī the ear-roots; Sugandhā the nose, and Carcikā the upper lip. (Verse 21.) In simple words: Kālī on the cheeks, Śaṅkarī at the ear-roots, sweet-fragrance goddess on the nose, Carcikā on the upper lip — every feature covered.

passages.mula:
अधरे चाऽमृतकला जिह्वायां तु सरस्वती ।
दन्तान् रक्षतु कौमारी कण्ठमध्ये तु चण्डिका ॥२२॥
passages.primaryEn: Amṛtakalā on the lower lip, Sarasvatī on the tongue; may Kaumārī guard the teeth, and Caṇḍikā the throat's middle. (Verse 22.) Combined with the variant note: some books read 'protect' (pātu) for 'guard', 'throat-region' for 'throat-middle', and 'Śāṅkarī' for 'Śaṅkarī' — small music-changes in the same prayer.

passages.mula:
घण्टिकां चित्रघण्टा च महामाया चं तालुके ।
कामाक्षी चिबुकं रक्षेद्वाचं मे सर्वमङ्गला ॥२३॥
passages.primaryEn: Citra-ghaṇṭā at the throat-bell, Mahāmāyā at the palate; may Kāmākṣī guard the chin, and Sarvamaṅgalā my speech. (Verse 23.) Combined with the commentaries: 'at the nostrils' means at the nose-holes (while later 'nose' alone means the nose-bridge); 'lower' means the lower lip. The Hindi prayer repeats verses 20–23 limb by limb: three-eyed one at brow-centre guards brows; death-bell at nose guards nostrils; conch-lady in both eyes guards eyes; door-keeper in both ears guards ears (20); Kālikā on cheeks, Śaṅkarī at ear-roots, Sugandhā on nose, Carcikā on upper lip guard each in turn (21); nectar-digit on lower lip, Sarasvatī on tongue, Kaumārī on teeth, Caṇḍikā mid-throat guard each (22); bell-pictured goddess at throat-bell, Great Illusion at palate, love-eyed goddess at chin, all-blessing goddess on speech guard each (23).

passages.mula:
ग्रीवायां भद्रकाली च पृष्ठवंशे धनुर्धरी ।
नीलग्रीवा बहिः कण्ठे नलिकां नलकूबरी ॥२४॥
passages.primaryEn: Bhadrakālī at the neck, Dhanurdharī on the spine; Nīlagrīvā outside the throat, Nalakūbarī at the windpipe. (Verse 24.) In simple words the guard moves to neck and back: kindly-Kālī on the neck, bow-bearer on the spine, blue-throated one on the throat's outside, Kubera's lady at the windpipe.

passages.mula:
खड्गधारिण्युभौ स्कन्धौं बाहू मे वज्रधारिणी ।
हस्तयोर्दण्डिनी रक्षेदम्बिका चाङ्गुलीषु च ॥२५॥
passages.primaryEn: May sword-bearer guard both shoulders, Vajradhāriṇī my arms; may Daṇḍinī guard the hands, and Ambikā the fingers. (Verse 25.) Combined with the commentaries: 'windpipe' means the throat-tube; the throat's outer part is the outer throat. 'Arm' means shoulder-to-elbow, 'hand' means elbow-to-fingertips — so each goddess knows exactly her stretch. The Hindi prayer repeats: Bhadrakālī guards the neck, bow-bearer the spine, blue-throated the outer throat, Nalakūbarī the windpipe (24); sword-bearer both shoulders, thunderbolt-bearer both my arms (25, continued next).

passages.mula:
दोनों हाथों में अवस्थित दण्डिनी दोनों हाथों की तथा अङ्गुलियों में अवस्थित
अम्बिका अलियों की रक्षा करें ॥२५॥
passages.primaryEn: Daṇḍinī stationed in both hands guards both hands, and Ambikā stationed in the fingers guards the fingers. (Verse 25, Hindi, with variant note.) Combined with the variant: some books read 'may the sword-lady guard the shoulders' — same guard, slightly different music.

passages.mula:
नखाञ्छूलेश्वरी रक्षेत्कुक्षौ रक्षेन्नलेश्वरी ।
स्तनौ रक्षेन्महादेवी मनः शोकविनाशिनी ॥२६॥
passages.primaryEn: May Śūleśvarī guard the nails, Naleśvarī the belly; Mahādevī the breasts, and Śokavināśinī the mind. (Verse 26.) In simple words: spear-lady on the nails, belly-goddess on the belly, Great Goddess on the breasts, grief-destroyer on the mind.

passages.mula:
हृदयं ललिता देवी ह्युदरे शूलधारिणी ।
नाभिं च कामिनी रक्षेद् गुह्यं गुह्येश्वरी तथा ॥२७॥
passages.primaryEn: Lalitā the heart, Śūladhāriṇī the belly; Kāminī the navel, and Guhyeśvarī the secret part. (Verse 27.) In simple words: the lovely one guards the heart, the spear-holder the stomach, the loving one the navel, the secret-lady the secret place.

passages.mula:
भूतनाथा च मेद्रं च गुद महिषवाहिनी ।
कट्यां भगवती रक्षेज्जानुनी विन्ध्यवासिनी ॥२८॥
passages.primaryEn: Bhūtanāthā the generative organ, Mahiṣavāhinī the anus; Bhagavatī the waist, Vindhyavāsinī the knees. (Verse 28, with the next verse quoted.) Combined with the old note: 'Mahābalā is declared at the shanks, Vināyakī between the knees, Nārasiṃhī at the ankles, Amitaujasī on the foot-top' (verse 29) — the guard-list marches down the legs.

passages.mula:
पादाङ्गलीः श्रीधरी च' पादाधस्तलवासिनी ।
नखान्दंष्ट्राः कराली च' केशांश्चैवोर्ध्वकेशिनी ॥३०॥
passages.primaryEn: Śrīdharī the toes, Talavāsinī dwelling under the feet; Karālī the toenails and teeth, and Ūrdhvakeśinī the hair. (Verse 30, with verse 31 quoted.) Combined with the commentaries: 'dweller at the foot' is one phrase, 'under-dweller' means underworld-dweller; 'under the feet' and 'underworld-dwelling' are separate words. Then verse 31: Kauberī in the hair-pores, Vāgīśvarī on the skin — and Pārvatī in blood, marrow, fat, flesh, bone and medulla. Guptavatī adds: Mahābalā is 'declared' — famous from the ancient lore-books — as the epithet of the great-strong Goddess. Pradīpa adds the old approved readings and the comforting rule: just as one goddess guarding two stations is no fault, two goddesses guarding one station is equally fine — which is why both toenails and teeth get Karālī.

passages.mula:
स्थानद्वयरक्षकत्वं न विरुध्यते तथैव देवताद्वयस्यैकस्थाननिरूपितरक्षकत्वे
बाधकाभाव इत्यभिप्रायेण नखान्दंष्ट्राः कराली चेत्युक्तम्॥३०॥३१॥
passages.primaryEn: The reasoning why one station may hold two guards and one guard two stations — so Karālī guards both toenails and teeth without contradiction. (Explanation of verses 30–31.) In simple words the commentators settle the doubt: sharing guard-duty, in either direction, breaks no rule — a mother can watch two children, and two mothers can watch one child.

passages.mula:
रक्षा करें। रक्त, मज्जा, वसा, मांस, हड्डी एवं मेद में अवस्थित होकर पार्वती
रक्त, मज्जा, वसा, मांस, हड्डी एवं मेद की रक्षा करें ।। ३१ ।।
passages.primaryEn: Kauberī in the hair-pores guards the pores, Vāgīśvarī on the skin guards the skin; Pārvatī dwelling in blood, marrow, fat, flesh, bone and medulla guards them all. (Verse 31, Hindi, with variants.) Combined with the variant list: some books read Kuleśvarī, 'in the heart', 'in the belly', 'at the navel', 'Pūtanā-Kāmikā for the organ', 'at the anus', 'giver of all desired boons', 'bright ones on the foot-top', 'may Śrī guard the toes', 'Karālī of nails and fangs'. Then the Hindi prayer of verses 28–31: Bhūtanāthā, buffalo-rider, Bhagavatī and Vindhya-dweller guard organ, anus, waist and both knees (28); declared Mahābalā the shanks, Vināyakī between knees, Nārasiṃhī the ankles, mighty Amitaujasī the foot-top (29); Śrīdharī the toes, under-feet-dweller the soles, Karālī the toenails and teeth, sky-haired one the hair (30); pore-dweller Kauberī the pores, speech-lady Vāgīśvarī the skin (31, continued).

passages.mula:
आन्त्राणि कालरात्रिश्च पित्तं च मुकुटेश्वरी ।
पद्मावती पद्मकोशे कफे चूडामणिस्तथा ॥३२॥
passages.primaryEn: Kālarātri the entrails, Mukuṭeśvarī the bile; Padmāvatī in the lotus-cave, and Cūḍāmaṇi in phlegm. (Verse 32.) Combined with the commentaries: 'in the lotus-cave' — the lotus is the heart and such; the goddess stationed in the breath dwelling there guards that breath, say some. Others say, since breath-guarding comes later, 'lotus-cave' here means the heart itself, as the scripture calls the heart 'like a lotus-cave, facing down'. Cūḍāmaṇi is the goddess famed in the Raktāsura-killing.

passages.mula:
चाप्यधोमुखम्' इति श्रुत्युक्तं हृदयमेव पद्मकोशशब्देन ग्राह्यमित्यपरे ।
चूडामणिनाम्नी देवता रक्तासुरवधे प्रसिद्धा ।।३२॥
passages.primaryEn: The heart itself, called 'lotus-cave facing down' by scripture, is what the name means here — and Cūḍāmaṇi is famed from the Raktāsura battle. (Verse 32, explanation.) In simple words the debate is settled gently: whether breath or heart, the Mother's guard covers the chest's innermost core.

passages.mula:
अवस्थित होकर मुकुटेश्वरी पित्त की, पद्मकोश में अवस्थित होकर पद्मावती
पद्मकोश की तथा कफ में अवस्थित होकर चूडामणि कफ की रक्षा करें ॥३२॥
passages.primaryEn: Kālarātri dwelling in the entrails guards them; Mukuṭeśvarī in bile guards bile; Padmāvatī in the lotus-cave guards it; Cūḍāmaṇi in phlegm guards phlegm. (Verse 32, Hindi.) In simple words the inner organs get their guards too — entrails, bile, heart-cave, phlegm — nothing inside left unwatched.

passages.mula:
ज्वालामुखी नखज्वालामभेद्या सर्वसन्धिषु ।
शुक्रं ब्रह्माणि मे रक्षेच्छायां छत्रेश्वरी तथा ॥३३॥
passages.primaryEn: Jvālāmukhī at the nail-flames, Abhedyā in all the joints; may Brāhmī guard my semen, and Chatreśvarī my shadow. (Verse 33.) In simple words: flame-faced goddess on the nails' glow, unbreakable goddess in every joint, Brahmā's power on vitality, umbrella-lady on the shadow.

passages.mula:
अहङ्कारं मनो बुद्धि रक्ष मे धर्मचारिणि
प्राणापानौ तथा व्यानसमानोदानमेव च ॥३४॥
passages.primaryEn: Ego, mind and intellect guard for me, O follower of righteousness — and the five breaths: prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, samāna, udāna. (Verse 34, with variant.) Combined with the variant: some books read 'O holder of righteousness' (dharmadhāriṇī) for 'O follower of righteousness'.

passages.mula:
यशः कीर्ति च लक्ष्मीं च सदा रक्षतु चक्रिणी ।
गोत्रमिन्द्राणि मे रक्षेत्पशून्मे रक्ष चण्डिके ॥३५॥
passages.primaryEn: Fame, glory and fortune — may Cakriṇī always guard; O Indrāṇī, guard my family-line; O Caṇḍikā, guard my cattle. (Verse 35.) Combined with the commentaries: here 'mind' means the whole inner mind-stuff (so the mind has four parts with the heart — no repetition with verse 26's grief-destroyer; or read it as 'She who destroys the mind's grief'). The five breaths are named in one breath as a group. Pradīpa adds: 'nail-flame' is the glow living in nails; the Unbreakable goddess stationed in all joints guards all joints; 'O Brāhmī, guard my vitality.' On verse 34's address the word 'you' is silently supplied, and the command runs in second person; on 35 too. The Hindi prayer continues: flame-faced on nail-glow, Unbreakable in all joints, Brāhmī on vitality, umbrella-lady on shadow (33); follower-of-righteousness on ego, mind, intellect and all five breaths (34). Then a caution: some copies add two extra verses here (thunderbolt-handed guarding breath; Yoginī in taste-form-smell-sound-touch; Nārāyaṇī guarding goodness-passion-darkness; Vārāhī guarding life, Vaiṣṇavī guarding duty) — but the ancients never took them, so they stay out of the original.

passages.mula:
पुत्रान् रक्षेन्महालक्ष्मीर्भार्यां रक्षतु भैरवी ।
मार्ग क्षेमकरी रक्षेविजया सर्वतः स्थितां ॥३६॥
passages.primaryEn: May Mahālakṣmī guard sons, Bhairavī the wife; Kṣemakarī the road, Vijayā dwelling everywhere. (Verse 36, with variants.) Combined with the variants: some read 'wealth and learning' for 'sons'; and some carry a longer road-verse — 'guard the path well, guard the road with welfare; Mahālakṣmī at the king's door, Vijayā dwelling everywhere'.

passages.mula:
रक्षाहीनं तु यत्स्थानं वर्जितं कवचेन तु ।
तत्सर्वं रक्ष मे देवी जयन्ती पापनाशिनी ॥३७॥
passages.primaryEn: Whatever station lacks guard, left out of the armour — all that guard for me, O Goddess, O Jayantī, destroyer of sins. (Verse 37, with verse 38 quoted.) Combined with the old note: 'if he wishes his own good, let him not take one step without the armour' — always wrapped in the Kavaca, wherever he goes. In simple words the devotee adds a safety net: Mother, any spot this long list may have missed — cover that too, O ever-victorious sin-destroyer.

passages.mula:
तत्र तत्रार्थलाभश्च विजयः सार्वकामिकः ।
यं यं चिन्तयते कामं तं तं प्राप्नोति निश्चितम् ॥३९॥
passages.primaryEn: There and there is gain of aims, and victory fulfilling all desires; whatever wish he thinks of, that he surely obtains. (Verse 39.) In simple words the fruit begins: wherever the armour-wearer goes, profit follows; victory that fulfils every wish follows; every thought-wish comes true — guaranteed.

passages.mula:
परमैश्वर्यमतुलं प्राप्स्यते भूतले पुमान् ।
निर्भयो जायते मर्त्यः सङ्ग्रामेष्वपराजितः ॥४०॥
passages.primaryEn: Unmatched supreme lordship he shall win on earth; fearless becomes the mortal, undefeated in battles. (Verse 40.) In simple words: peerless power on this earth, zero fear, and no defeat in any fight — that is the Kavaca-wearer's fortune.

passages.mula:
त्रैलोक्ये तु भवेत्पूज्यः कवचेनावृतः पुमान् ।
इदं तु देव्याः कवचं देवानामपि दुर्लभम् ॥४१॥
passages.primaryEn: Worshipped in all three worlds becomes the man wrapped in the armour; and this armour of the Goddess is hard even for gods to get. (Verse 41.) Combined with the commentaries: verses 36–37 name the fruit of wearing; verse 38 ('not one step without it') means: without the worn armour — don't move an inch if you want your own good; never let a moment pass without the Goddess in mind. The old Purāṇa line is quoted: sleeping, standing, walking, talking, delighting in food — always chant the Goddess, and you are freed from bondage. So after teaching the rule, the hymn tells the fruit: wrapped, wherever he goes (38–41).

passages.mula:
कीर्तयेत्सततं देवीं स वै मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥ इति ॥
इत्युपदिश्य फलं कथयति कवचेनेति ॥ ३८॥ ३९॥४०॥४१॥
passages.primaryEn: 'Always chant the Goddess — sleeping, standing, walking, talking, delighting in food — and you are freed from bondage,' say the Purāṇas. So taught the rule, now the fruit is told. (Verse 38's seal.) In simple words: remembrance has no off-hours — chant moving, resting, eating — and every bondage breaks.

passages.mula:
भयरहित हो जाता है। कवच से सुरक्षित पुरुष तीनों लोकों में पूजनीय होता
है। देवी का यह कवच देवताओं के लिये भी दुर्लभ है ।।४० ।।४१ ॥
passages.primaryEn: He becomes free of fear; worshipped in the three worlds, the armour-wrapped man; this armour of the Goddess is rare even for gods. (Verses 40–41, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats the promise with joy: no fear, honoured in heaven-earth-underworld, holding something even gods can hardly get.

passages.mula:
यः पठेत्प्रयतो नित्यं त्रिसन्ध्यं श्रद्धयान्वितः ।
दैवी कला भवेत्तस्य त्रैलोक्ये चापराजितः ॥४२ ॥
passages.primaryEn: Whoever reads with discipline, daily, at all three twilights, full of faith — divine lustre comes to him, and in all three worlds he is undefeated. (Verse 42.) In simple words: dawn, noon, dusk — read with rule and faith every day, and you shine with goddess-glow, unbeaten anywhere.

passages.mula:
जीवेद्वर्षशतं साग्रमपमृत्युविवर्जितः ।
नश्यन्ति व्याधयः सर्वे लूताविस्फोटकादयः ॥४३॥
passages.primaryEn: He lives a hundred years and more, free of sudden death; all diseases perish — skin-blisters, smallpox and the rest. (Verse 43.) In simple words: full lifespan past a hundred, no accidents, and every illness — from rashes to poxes — wiped out.

passages.mula:
स्थावरं जङ्गमं चापि कृत्रिमं चापि यद्विषम् ।
अभिचाराणि सर्वाणि मन्त्रयन्त्राणि भूतले ॥४४॥
passages.primaryEn: Stationary poisons, moving poisons, and man-made poisons too; all black-magic rites on earth, all spells and diagrams. (Verse 44.) In simple words the protection-list widens: plant poisons, snake poisons, lab-made poisons, every evil rite and every magic circle on earth.

passages.mula:
भूचराः खेचराश्चैव जलजाश्चौपदेशिकाः ।
सहजाः कुलजा माला डाकिनी शाकिनी तथा ॥४५॥
passages.primaryEn: Earth-roamers and sky-roamers, water-born and teaching-born; inborn and family-born troops — Ḍākinī and Śākinī too. (Verse 45.) In simple words: every creepy host is named — crawlers, flyers, water-spirits, spell-learnt ones, inborn and clan-bound hordes, Ḍākinīs and Śākinīs.

passages.mula:
अन्तरिक्षचरा घोरा डाकिन्यश्च महाबलाः ।
ग्रहभूतपिशाचाश्च यक्षगन्धर्वराक्षसाः ॥४६॥
passages.primaryEn: Sky-roaming terrors, and hugely strong Ḍākinīs; planets, ghosts, goblins, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, demons. (Verse 46.) In simple words: sky-terrors, mighty witch-hosts, seizure-spirits, ghosts, goblins, nature-spirits, musicians of heaven, man-eaters — the whole roster.

passages.mula:
ब्रह्मराक्षसवेतालाः कूष्माण्डा भैरवादयः ।
नश्यन्ति दर्शनात्तस्य कवचे हृदि संस्थिते ॥४७॥
passages.primaryEn: Brahma-demons, vampires, Kūṣmāṇḍas, Bhairavas and the rest — perish at his very sight, once the armour rests in his heart. (Verse 47.) In simple words: the darkest ones — brahmin-ghosts, corpse-risers, imp hordes, fierce Bhairava troops — melt away just by looking at the man whose heart holds the Kavaca.

passages.mula:
मानोन्नतिर्भवेद्राज्ञस्तेजोवृद्धिकरं परम् ।
यशसा वर्धते सोऽपि कीर्तिमण्डितभूतले ॥४८॥
passages.primaryEn: The king honours him more and more; it grows supreme brilliance; and he too grows with fame, garlanding the earth with glory. (Verse 48.) Combined with the commentaries: 'stationary' poison means aconite and such; 'moving' means snakes and the like; 'man-made' means mixed poisons like honey-and-ghee in equal measure gone wrong. 'Family-born' and the rest are classes of dark deities; 'teaching-born' are petty spirits perfected by mere instruction. 'Divine lustre' is the glow of pure consciousness. The Hindi prayer repeats verses 42–48 whole: thrice-daily faithful reading gives goddess-glow and three-world victory (42); hundred-plus years, no sudden death, all diseases dead (43); then every poison — plant, snake-scorpion, and mixed things like opium and oil blends — every spell, diagram and black rite on earth; crawlers, flyers, water-born, teaching-born, inborn, clan troops, garland-Ḍākinīs, Śākinīs, sky-terrors, mighty Ḍākinīs, planets, ghosts, goblins, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, demons, brahmin-ghosts, vampires, Kuṣmāṇḍas, Bhairavas — all perish merely at the sight of the armour-hearted man; and that best of men rises in royal honour, blazes with supreme glow, and grows in fame that garlands the earth (44–48).

passages.mula:
जपेत्सप्तशतीं चण्डीं कृत्वा तु कवचं पुरा ।
यावद्भूमण्डलं धत्ते सशैलवनकाननम् ॥४९ ॥
passages.primaryEn: Having first worn the armour, let him chant the Seven-hundred Cāṇḍī — as long as the earth-disc holds mountains, forests and woods. (Verse 49.) In simple words the rule of order: first wear the Kavaca, then chant the Saptashatī — and the fruit lasts as long as the earth itself stands with its mountains and forests.

passages.mula:
तावत्तिष्ठति मेदिन्यां सन्ततिः पुत्रपौत्रिकी ।
देहान्ते परमं स्थानं यत्सुरैरपि दुर्लभम् ॥५०॥
passages.primaryEn: So long shall his line of sons and grandsons stand on earth; after the body's end, the supreme station, hard even for gods. (Verse 50.) In simple words: your children and grandchildren stay rooted on earth as long as the world lasts — and after death, you reach the highest place, which even gods find hard to win.

passages.mula: प्राप्नोति पुरुषो नित्यं महामायाप्रसादतः ॥५१॥
passages.primaryEn: That supreme station the man surely wins, always, by Mahāmāyā's grace. (Verse 51.) In simple words: not by effort alone — by the Great Mother Illusion's own grace, surely and forever.

passages.mula: ।। इति श्रीदेवीकवचं समाप्तम् ।।
passages.primaryEn: Thus ends the holy armour of the Goddess. Combined with the two closers: the Kavaca must be worn first and then the Saptashatī chanted — that order itself proves the armour belongs to the Caṇḍī recitation as its limb; earlier the hymn spoke other side-fruits too, but by the law of side-desires those extra practices stand outside without fault. 'As long as the earth-disc' is praise-speech like 'full-perfection fruit-speech'. 'First' means first in time only — and since no gaplessness is taught here, the night-hymn wrap-around is explained elsewhere ('read the night-hymn first'); by Vedic order (beginning-middle-end words and the step-word), the night-hymn comes first and the nine-lettered mantra sits before it. So too the Argala's 'having read this hymn, let man read the great hymn' teaches only limb-and-whole kinship — as with 'having eaten today, he goes tomorrow', the -having-done form allows a gap, so the Vedic order stands unharmed and no gap breaks it. By the drawing-together rule (as with the ten-callers' calls and chants), the order is fixed: Kavaca, Argala, nine-lettered, night-hymn, Caṇḍī-praise; and after counting praise-and-chant come Goddess-hymn, nine-lettered and mysteries, in order. (Verses 49–51, Guptavatī's seal on the Kavaca explanation.)

passages.mula:
विशेषेणैव जन्तूनां नात्र सन्देहकारणम्' ॥ इति ।
सूतसंहितोक्तेश्च।।५०॥५१॥
passages.primaryEn: Quoted scriptures confirm: 'whom the Self chooses, by him It is won' — and 'who knows this power of illusion conquers death, crosses sin, reaches deathlessness' — and 'I Myself speak this, tasted by gods and men' — and 'Pārvatī is the supreme wisdom, giver of Brahman-wisdom.' (Pradīpa's seal, verses 50–51.) In simple words the old books all agree: the Supreme chooses Its own; knowing the Mother's power means victory over death, sin and mortality itself.

passages.mula:
कवचेऽस्मिन्सार्धपञ्चाशत्संख्याश्लोकसङ्ग्रहः ।।
।। इति प्रदीपव्याख्याने कवचव्याख्या समाप्ता ।।
passages.primaryEn: Whoever first reads the armour and then reads the Saptashatī or Caṇḍī — his line of sons and grandsons stays on earth as long as the earth-disc holds mountains, forests and woods. And after the body's end, by holy Mahāmāyā's grace he surely reaches that eternal supreme station, hard even for gods. (Verses 49–51, Hindi.) One book adds 'he gains the supreme form and rejoices with Śiva' — but since most books don't agree, it stays out of the original. Then the Argala hymn begins: its seer is Viṣṇu, metre anuṣṭup, deity great Lakṣmī, purpose — pleasing Mother Jagadambā as a limb of the Saptashatī chant; and Mārkaṇḍeya speaks.

passages.mula:
जयन्ती मङ्गला काली भद्रकाली कपालिनी ।
दुर्गा क्षमा शिवा धात्री स्वाहा स्वधा नमोऽस्तु ते ॥१॥
passages.primaryEn: Jayantī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, Kapālinī; Durgā, Kṣamā, Śivā, Dhātrī — Svāhā, Svadhā, salutation to You! (Argala verse 1.) Combined with the commentaries: the grammar joins possessive endings simply ('victorious one' and the rest); then the praise begins with the Goddess aimed at by meditation, listing Her qualities fit for focus. Jayantī: the topmost victor — the Mother as Brahman veiled by the three qualities, cause of all. Maṅgalā: She who takes away devotees' creeping through birth-and-death and grants freedom — 'his breaths do not depart' says scripture. Kālī: She who swallows all this at world-end — 'Brahman and warriorhood both become His food, with Death as sauce' says scripture. Bhadrakālī: She who takes goodness and joy to give devotees, 'giver of joy' as the secret lore says. Kapālinī: skull means head-bone (says the dictionary) — She who killed Brahmā and the rest and roams at world-end holding their skulls; or lotus-universe in hand; the secret lore hails Her 'lotus-universe-handed supreme Kapālinī'. Durgā: reached with pain through yoga, ritual and worship — 'that Durgā, hard to reach' says the Atharvaśiras. Kṣamā: She who bears all faults of devotees and others, being Mother, overflowing with mercy. Śivā: Herself pure consciousness — as the Sūta Saṃhitā sings at length: the changeless, ever-blissful awareness, destroyer of worldliness, supreme Goddess, one with Śiva, maker of good. Dhātrī: holder of the whole expanse — 'I move with Rudras and Vasus, I bear Mitra-Varuṇa, Indra-Agni and the Aśvins' says scripture. Svāhā feeds the gods, Svadhā feeds the ancestors. O possessor of all these great qualities — to You, salutation alone; for serving such a One in full, who has the strength? The Hindi prayer begins: Mārkaṇḍeya ṛṣi, teaching his students the Goddess's praise, said — Jayantī 1, Maṅgalā 2 … (continued).

passages.mula:
५ दुर्गा ६ क्षमा ७ शिवा ८ धात्री ९ स्वाहा १० तथा स्वधा ११ इन नामों
से प्रसिद्ध हे देवि ! तुम्हें मेरा नमस्कार प्राप्त हो।।१।।
passages.primaryEn: This opening passage salutes the Goddess by Her beloved names — Durgā, Kṣamā (Forgiveness), Śivā, Dhātrī (Nourisher), Svāhā and Svadhā — and offers Her respectful salutation. In simple words: O Mother, You are famous under all these holy names, and I bow to You. (The next passage explains what each name means.)

passages.mula:
विशेष - १. जयन्ती - जयति सर्वोत्कर्षेण वर्तते या सा जयन्ती। जो
सबसे उत्कृष्ट हो उसे जयनती कहते हैं। २. मङ्गला - मङ्गं सर्पणं भक्तानां लाति
इति मङ्गला । जो भक्तों को मङ्ग देती है वह मङ्गला है। मङ्ग का अर्थ सर्पण
अर्थात् गति है। अतः भक्तों को शुभगति देने वाली मङ्गला कहलाती है।
passages.primaryEn: This passage opens the meanings of the Goddess's eleven names, and combined with the note attached to it, all eleven are: 1. Jayantī — She who wins over everything, the highest victor. 2. Maṅgalā — She who carries Her devotees to good fortune and swift progress. 3. Kālī — She who swallows the whole world at the end of time. 4. Bhadrakālī — She who gives welfare and goodness to Her devotees. 5. Kapālinī — She who holds the skull-bowl. 6. Durgā — She who is reached only with great effort through yoga, worship and hard practice, and whose songs are sung in times of trouble. 7. Kṣamā — the Mother whose heart overflows with mercy, so She forgives all Her children's faults by nature. 8. Śivā — the giver of goodness, the Mother of the world, Herself pure consciousness. 9. Dhātrī — She who holds and feeds the entire universe. 10. Svāhā — the power by which the gods receive their share of every sacrifice. 11. Svadhā — the power by which departed ancestors receive offerings of food and water. In short: this first verse describes the Mother's complete work — winning, blessing, protecting, feeding gods, ancestors and devotees — and is itself treated as a great mantra.

passages.mula:
मधुकैटभविद्राविविधातृवरदे नमः ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥२॥
passages.primaryEn: Salutation to Her who drove away Madhu and Kaiṭabha and blessed Brahmā! Then comes the refrain repeated through the whole hymn: Grant me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother who chased away the demons Madhu-Kaiṭabha and gave a boon to Brahmā, I bow to You — give me spiritual beauty, victory, and good name, and kill my enemies. The deep meaning of the refrain (explained in the commentaries ahead): 'beauty' means the supreme Self shining in the heart; 'victory' means the treasure of the Vedas; 'fame' means the glory born of true wisdom; and the 'foes' to be killed are lust, anger and the inner enemies.

passages.mula:
महिषासुरनिर्नाशविधात्री वरदे नमः ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥३॥
passages.primaryEn: Salutation to Her who brings about the total destruction of Mahiṣāsura and grants boons! Grant me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother who finished the buffalo-demon Mahiṣa completely and who blesses Her children, I bow to You — bless me with beauty, victory and good name, and destroy the enemies within and without.

passages.mula:
वन्दिताध्रियुगे देवि देवि सौभाग्यदायिनि ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥४॥
passages.primaryEn: O Goddess whose twin feet are worshipped by all, O giver of good fortune — grant me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. Combined with the three commentaries: the grammar joins 'She who scatters (the demons) and also grants Brahmā's boon' into one; 'beauty' here means three things at once — the charm that wins over Her own people, the terror She strikes into Her enemies, and divine loveliness itself. The Pradīpa retells the beloved story from the Devībhāgavata — Brahmā praised Her to kill Madhu-Kaiṭabha and She blessed him — and opens the refrain's inner meaning: beauty is the supreme Self to be known, victory is the wealth of Veda and sacred memory, fame is the glory born of Self-knowledge, and the foes are lust, anger and their brood. On verse 4 it notes Her feet are worshipped even by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and the word 'Devi' is repeated purely out of overflowing devotion.

passages.mula:
हे देवि! तुम्हें नमस्कार है। तुम रूप दो जय दो यश दो तथा काम क्रोधादि
शत्रुओं का नाश करो ॥ २॥
passages.primaryEn: O Goddess, salutation to You! Give me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy enemies like lust and anger. (Verse 2.) In simple words this is the Hindi prayer of the same verse: the devotee bows and begs the Mother who killed Madhu-Kaiṭabha for inner beauty, success, good name, and freedom from anger and desire.

passages.mula:
इस श्लोक के पूर्व कुछ प्रतियों में-
जय त्वं देवि चामुण्डे जय भूतार्तिहारिणि ।
जय सर्वगते देवि कालरात्रि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
passages.primaryEn: Some prayer-books carry one extra verse before this point — 'Victory to You, O Cāmuṇḍā, remover of the sufferings of beings! Victory to the all-pervading Goddess! Salutation to Kālarātri!' — but the editors explain honestly: this verse is not accepted by tradition and no ancient commentator explains it, so it is not counted in the original hymn. Then the Hindi prayer continues: O destroyer of Mahiṣāsura, giver of boons, salutation! Give beauty, victory, fame, destroy foes (verse 3). O Goddess with worshipped twin feet, giver of fortune — give beauty, victory, fame, destroy foes (verse 4).

passages.mula:
रक्तबीजवधे देवि चण्डमुण्डविनाशिनि ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥५॥
passages.primaryEn: O Goddess who brought about the killing of Raktabīja, O destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa — grant me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother who killed the blood-seed demon (from whose every drop of blood new demons sprang) and finished Caṇḍa-Muṇḍa, I bow — bless me with beauty, victory and fame, and kill my inner foes.

passages.mula:
अचिन्त्यरूपचरिते सर्वशत्रुविनाशिनि ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: O Goddess whose form and deeds are beyond thought, O destroyer of all foes — grant me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother whose shape and actions no mind can fully grasp, who wipes out every enemy, I bow — bless and protect me.

passages.mula:
नतेभ्यः सर्वदा भक्तया चण्डिके प्रणताय में ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: O Caṇḍikā, to those bowed with devotion forever, and to bowed-down me — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother, to all Your devotees who bow with love at all times, and to me too who bows before You — give beauty, victory, fame, and destroy our foes.

passages.mula:
स्तुवद्र्यो भक्तिपूर्वं त्वां चण्डिके व्याधिनाशिनि ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥८॥
passages.primaryEn: O Caṇḍikā, destroyer of diseases, to those who praise You first with devotion — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. Combined with the four commentaries: the grammar joins 'the killing happened through Her' into one word for verse 5; verse 6's 'beyond thought' is backed by the Upaniṣad lines — 'words turn back from It' and 'the overseer in the highest heaven knows, or perhaps does not know'; verse 7 simply connects — to the ever-bowed devotees and to bowed me, give beauty and the rest; verse 8 works the same way. One caution from Pradīpa: some books insert a verse about Śumbha here, but it is a wrong reading — the ancients never explain it and old books don't carry it. The Hindi prayer then repeats verses 5–8 as devotion: killer of Raktabīja and Caṇḍa-Muṇḍa; beyond-thought destroyer of foes; giver to all bowing devotees and to me; healer of diseases worshipped with love — give beauty, victory, fame, destroy lust, anger and all foes.

passages.mula:
चण्डिके सततं ये त्वामर्चयन्तीह भक्तितः ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥९॥
passages.primaryEn: O Caṇḍikā, to those who worship You here constantly with devotion — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: whoever serves You daily with a loving heart — bless them with beauty, victory, good name, and destroy their enemies.

passages.mula:
देहि सौभाग्यमारोग्यं देहि देवि परं सुखम् ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥१०॥
passages.primaryEn: Grant good fortune and health, O Goddess, grant supreme happiness — grant me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother, bless me with luck, a healthy body and the highest joy — and with beauty, victory, fame, and freedom from foes.

passages.mula:
विधेहि द्विषतां नाशं विधेहि बलमुच्चकैः ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥११॥
passages.primaryEn: Bring about the destruction of my haters; build up strength in me to the highest — grant me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother, finish those who hate me and fill me with towering strength — with beauty, victory, fame, and no enemies left.

passages.mula:
विधेहि देवि कल्याणं विधेहि विपुलां श्रियम् ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥१२॥
passages.primaryEn: Bring welfare, O Goddess; grant vast noble wealth — grant me beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother, make my life blessed and fill my home with plenty — with beauty, victory, fame, and destroyed foes.

passages.mula:
विद्यावन्तं यशस्वन्तं लक्ष्मीवन्तं जनं कुरु ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥१३॥
passages.primaryEn: Make (Your) person learned, famous and wealthy — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother, make Your devotee — make me — full of learning, shining with good name and blessed with wealth — with beauty, victory, fame, and no inner enemies.

passages.mula:
प्रचण्डदैत्यदर्पप्ने चण्डिके प्रणताय मे ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥ १४॥
passages.primaryEn: O Caṇḍikā who crushes the pride of the terrible demons, to bowed-down me — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother who smashes the arrogance of the fiercest demons, I surrender before You — bless me with beauty, victory, fame, and destroy my foes.

passages.mula:
चतुर्भुजे चतुर्वक्त्रसंस्तुते परमेश्वरि ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥१५॥
passages.primaryEn: O supreme Lady praised by the four-faced one (Brahmā) and the four-armed one (Viṣṇu) — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. Combined with the commentaries: verses 9–12 each silently add 'to those who worship' / 'to me' — supply it while chanting. 'Your person' in verse 13 means Your devotee — me. The Hindi prayer repeats the same devotion across verses 9–15: to constant worshippers; luck, health and highest joy to me; ruin of haters and towering strength in me; welfare and vast wealth; learning, fame and riches for Your servant; shelter for surrendered me before the demon-pride-crusher; praise from Brahmā and Viṣṇu — always closing with: give beauty, victory, fame, and destroy lust, anger and all foes.

passages.mula:
भुजाओं वाली हे परमेश्वरी ! तुम रूप दो, जय दो, यश दो तथा काम क्रोधादि
शत्रुओं का नाश करो ॥१५॥
passages.primaryEn: O supreme Lady with four arms, praised by four-faced Brahmā — give beauty, victory and fame, and destroy the foes like lust and anger. (Verse 15, Hindi prayer.) In simple words: the devotee pictures the Mother with four arms, hymned by Brahmā Himself, and begs for beauty, victory, fame and freedom from inner enemies.

passages.mula:
कृष्णेन संस्तुते देवि शश्वद्भक्तत्या तथाऽम्बिके ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥१६॥
passages.primaryEn: O Goddess hymned by Kṛṣṇa, O Ambikā, always with true devotion — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother whom Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself praises with steady love — I bow; bless me with beauty, victory, fame, and destroy my foes.

passages.mula:
हिमाचलसुतानाथपूजिते परमेश्वरि ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥ १७॥
passages.primaryEn: O supreme Lady worshipped by the Lord of Himālaya's daughter (Śiva, husband of Pārvatī) — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother worshipped even by Lord Śiva Himself — I bow; bless me with beauty, victory, fame, and destroy my foes.

passages.mula:
सुरासुरशिरोरत्ननिघृष्टचरणेऽम्बिके
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥१८॥
passages.primaryEn: O Ambikā whose feet are rubbed by the crown-jewels of gods and demons alike — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother before whose feet even gods and demons bow their jewelled crowns — I bow; bless me with beauty, victory, fame, and destroy my foes.

passages.mula:
इन्द्राणीपतिसद्भावपूजिते परमेश्वरि ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥१९॥
passages.primaryEn: O supreme Lady worshipped with true feeling by Indra, husband of Indrāṇī — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. Combined with the commentaries: Guptavatī tells the old Purāṇa story — Indra once hid long inside a lotus stalk in a lake, and regained his place only by worshipping the Goddess with a true heart; that is the 'true feeling' praised here. Pradīpa adds the inner hint of verse 18: when gods and demons bow together at one pair of feet, all hatred melts into oneness — a whisper of non-duality. The Hindi prayer repeats verses 16–19 with love: hymned by Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa; worshipped by Śiva; feet rubbed by gods' and demons' crowns; worshipped sincerely by Indra — always: give beauty, victory, fame, and destroy my lust, anger and foes.

passages.mula:
देव्याराधनेन पौलोम्या तत्स्थलं लब्धमिति पुराणेषु प्रसिद्धेः। इन्द्राणीपतिना
सद्भावेन पूजिते इति वा॥१९॥
passages.primaryEn: This passage continues the old Guptavatī explanation of verse 19: the Purāṇas famously tell how Indrāṇī’s husband Indra won back his lost place only through worship of the Goddess — worship with a true heart recovers even a lost heaven. (The three attached notes give Pradīpa’s verse-by-verse gist, the Hindi prayers of verses 16–19, and two variant readings.)

passages.mula:
देवि प्रचण्डदोर्दण्डदैत्यदर्पविनाशिनि ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥ २०॥
passages.primaryEn: O Goddess who destroys the pride of demons with strong staff-like arms — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother whose mighty arms smash demon arrogance — I bow; bless me with beauty, victory, fame, and destroy my foes.

passages.mula:
देवि भक्तजनोद्दामदत्तानन्दोदयेऽम्बिके ।
रूपं देहि जयं देहि यशो देहि द्विषो जहि ॥२१॥
passages.primaryEn: O Ambikā in whom the rise of bliss — liberation itself — is given to the finest among devotee folk — grant beauty, victory and fame, and destroy my foes. In simple words: O Mother who grants even final freedom to Her best devotees — I bow; bless me with beauty, victory, fame, and destroy my foes.

passages.mula:
पत्नीं मनोरमां देहि मनोवृत्तानुसारिणीम्।
तारिणीं दुर्गसंसारसागरस्य कुलोद्भवाम् ॥२२॥
passages.primaryEn: Grant a lovely wife who follows my heart's ways, who carries (souls) across the hard-to-cross ocean of worldly life, and who is born in a noble family. (Verse 22 — a householder's prayer.) Combined with the commentaries: 'she who ferries across' is compared to two famous mothers of story — Madālasā of the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, who ferried her son across, and Cūḍālā of the Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha, who ferried her husband across. So the verse begs: O Mother, bless me with a life-partner noble by birth, lovely, like-minded, and spiritually uplifting — one who helps me cross this ocean of birth and death. The Hindi prayer says the same with folded hands.

passages.mula:
इदं स्तोत्रं पठित्वा तु महास्तोत्रं पठेन्नरः ।
स तु सप्तशतीसङ्ख्यावरमाप्नोति सम्पदः ॥२३॥
passages.primaryEn: A man who, after reciting this hymn, recites the great hymn (the Saptashatī) — he obtains the excellent reward counted in Saptashatī numbers, along with riches. In simple words: chant the Argala first and then the Saptashatī, and you will surely receive the full fruit of the Saptashatī count plus abundant prosperity. The commentaries confirm: the 'great hymn' means the Saptashatī itself, which is the main hymn; this verse proves the Argala belongs to the Saptashatī family — so never skip it; the merit earned is countless, and it pours down as wealth too.

passages.mula: ।। इति देव्या अर्गलास्तुतिः समाप्ता ।।
passages.primaryEn: Thus ends the Argala praise of the Goddess. Combined with the closers: Guptavatī seals her explanation here, and Pradīpa underlines the rule — whoever chants the Saptashatī after this Argala hymn, and he alone, receives the fruit born of that count plus all riches. Therefore the Argala must always be read first — that is the final word.

passages.mula:
सिद्धिप्रतिबन्धकं पापमर्गलासदृशत्वादर्गला तन्नाशकस्तोत्रस्यापि लक्षणयार्गलेति
संज्ञा ।। २३।।
passages.primaryEn: Sin blocks success the way a bolt (argalā) bars a door — so the hymn that destroys it is itself called Argala. (Verse 23's seal.) In simple words: our sins stand like a wooden bolt across the door of blessings; this hymn smashes that bolt, and that is why its name is Argala, 'the unbolter'.

passages.mula:
त्रयोविंशतिसङ्ख्यानां श्लोकानामत्र सङ्ग्रहः ।
।। इति प्रदीपव्याख्याने अर्गलाविवरणम्।।
passages.primaryEn: Here is gathered twenty-three verses in count — thus ends the Argala explanation. Combined with the Hindi prayer: whoever reads this Argala hymn and then reads the great Saptashatī hymn will surely gain its finest fruit along with overflowing wealth.

passages.mula:
जपसङ्ख्या से जायमान उत्तम फल को प्राप्त करने के साथ ही प्रचुर सम्पत्ति
भी प्राप्त करता है ॥ २३॥
passages.primaryEn: Along with the finest fruit born of the Saptashatī count, the chanter also gains abundant wealth. (Verse 23, Hindi.) In simple words: read Argala, then Saptashatī — and receive both the supreme spiritual fruit and full material prosperity.

passages.mula:
ॐ अस्य श्रीकीलकमन्त्रस्य शिव ऋषिः, अनुष्टप छन्दः, श्रीमहासरस्वती
देवता, श्रीजगदम्बाप्रीत्यर्थं सप्तशतीपाठाङ्गत्वेन जपे विनियोगः ।
विशुद्धज्ञानदेहाय
श्रेयःप्राप्तिनिमित्ताय
ऋषिरुवार्च
त्रिवेदीदिव्यचक्षुषे ।
नमः सोमार्धधारिणे ॥१॥

सर्वमेतद्विजानीयान्मन्त्राणामभिकीलकम् ।
सोऽपि क्षेममवाप्नोति सततं जाप्यतत्परः ॥२॥

च। एतदेव विवृणोति। सिध्यन्तीति। एतेन चण्डीस्तवेन। नित्यमित्यादि भिन्नं
वाक्यम्। परब्रह्मापि स्तोत्रमात्रेणैव सिध्यतीत्यर्थः ।।२।।
passages.primaryEn: The seer asks: what did He say? All this — know that the Saptashatī hymn itself, which by its stated method destroys the curse-like bolt blocking all mantra success, is the un-bolter (abhikīlaka); worship it as such. And if you ask whether other mantra practices give no safety, that they surely can't be abandoned for this alone — the answer comes: even the man constantly busy chanting this Saptashatī hymn, plus the man busy with many other mantras, both reach all welfare. (Verse 2, with Pradīpa.) Combined with the Hindi: the Saptashatī hymn that removes the curse-bolt blocking mantra success must be fully known; yet one absorbed in other mantras' chanting also reaches welfare.

passages.mula:
सिद्धयन्त्युच्चाटनादीनि वस्तूनि सकलान्यपि ।
एतेन स्तुवतां देवी स्तोत्रमात्रेण सिद्धयति ॥३॥
passages.primaryEn: By this (hymn) expulsion-rites and all things succeed for those who praise the Goddess — by the hymn alone She is won. (Verse 3.) Combined with the commentaries: the man devoted to chanting finds even expulsion-rites and all hard-to-get things succeeding; and to men who chant only mantras without Saptashatī-reading, success by mere mantra-chant was already granted — now, to men who read only the Saptashatī without mantra-chanting either, the hymn grants every success by mere reading of this famed hymn: the Goddess Herself, of true-being-consciousness-bliss form, is pleased. The Hindi repeats: besides Saptashatī-reading, other mantras' chanting also fulfils expulsion and all aims — but those who praise with this hymn alone win the Goddess of blissful reality Herself. (Continued next.)

passages.mula:
केवल इस सप्तशती नामक स्तोत्र से ही स्तुति करने वाले हैं, उनके लिये तो
सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी भगवती सप्तशती मात्र से ही सिद्ध हो जातीं हैं।। ३॥
passages.primaryEn: Those who praise with this Saptashatī hymn alone win the blissful-reality Goddess Herself, by the hymn alone. (Verse 3, Hindi completion.) In simple words: other paths work, but this hymn by itself is enough to win Her — that is its special promise.

passages.mula:
न मन्त्रो नौषधं तत्र न किञ्चिदपि विद्यते ।
विना जाप्येन सिद्धयेत सर्वमुच्चाटनादिकम् ॥४॥
passages.primaryEn: No mantra there, no herb, nothing else at all is found — without any chanting, all expulsion-rites and the rest succeed. (Verse 4.) Combined with the commentaries: someone may fear — if the easy Caṇḍī-praise makes all hard-won lores useless, why keep them? The verse answers: for that man's success no other mantra is of use, no herb, no yoga-power or other means at all — yet without any mantra-chanting ritual, all expulsion rites and every wished-for work succeed by the hymn alone. So far: by Saptashatī-practice alone all welfare comes; and by other-mantra practice too all welfare comes — both paths are proved true. The Hindi repeats: readers of Saptashatī need no mantra, no herb, no other means — without chanting-rituals, all expulsion and all aims succeed by reading alone. (Continued next.)

passages.mula:
करने के विना ही (केवल पाठ मात्र से ही) उनके उच्चाटन आदि समस्त कार्य
सिद्ध) हो जाते हैं।।४।।
passages.primaryEn: Without chanting-rituals their expulsion-rites and all aims succeed — by reading alone. (Verse 4, Hindi completion.) In simple words: no herbs, no extra mantras, no instruments — just read, and everything succeeds.

passages.mula:
समग्राण्यपि सेत्स्यन्तिं लोकशङ्कामिमां हरः ।
कृत्वा निमन्त्रयामास सर्वमेवमिदं शुभम् ॥५॥
passages.primaryEn: To remove people's doubt about all the lores, Hara invited them — 'all this is wholly good.' (Verse 5.) Combined with Guptavatī: He invited — He thought it over and showed His thinking. 'All' means: once this bolt-making is done, the whole family of lores becomes good and fruitful — people fulfilled by mere Caṇḍī-praise alone may drop all other duty-wealth-desire-freedom scriptures without loss. So the bolt was built by Śiva to block praise-born successes, in order to keep the other lores meaningful — that is the sense of all four verses (2–5).

passages.mula:
सर्वाणि धर्मार्थकाममोक्षशास्त्राण्यत्यजन्। अतः कीलननिर्माणेन स्तवमात्रजन्यानां
सिद्धीनां प्रतिबन्धः शिवेनेतरविद्यासार्थक्यार्थ कृत इति श्लोकचतुष्काशयः ।।५ ॥
passages.primaryEn: The bolt was built by Śiva to block successes born of mere praise, so that the other lores keep their purpose — that is the sense of verses 2–5. (Explanation.) In simple words: the lock exists to protect the value of every other sacred science; without it, one easy hymn would empty all other paths.

passages.mula:
तानागतानाह। किमिति एवं वक्ष्यमाणप्रकारेणेदं सप्तशत्याख्यमेव शुभमिति अत्र
तानाहेति शेषः ।।५।।
passages.primaryEn: The people's two-sided doubt — 'both these paths exist, but which?' — Hara first removed by inviting them, as if to say: come, I shall clear this doubt. (Pradīpa on verse 5.) Combined with the Hindi: 'Can everything really succeed by Saptashatī alone, with no other chanting?' — holding this doubt of people's minds before Him, Lord Śiva thought it over and decided: this Saptashatī-hymn reading alone is best and most blesse.

passages.mula:
बुलाकर) भगवान शङ्कर ने विचार किया तथा यह सप्तशतीस्तोत्र पाठ ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ
एवं कल्याणप्रद है (ऐसा निर्णय दिया) ॥५॥
passages.primaryEn: Lord Śiva invited all, thought it over, and decided: reading this Saptashatī hymn alone is supreme and blessing-giving. (Verse 5, Hindi completion.) In simple words the doubt is settled from God's own mouth: this hymn alone is enough — and best.

passages.mula:
स्तोत्रं वै चण्डिकायास्तु तच्च गुह्यं चकार सः ।
समाप्तिर्न च पुण्यस्य तां यथावन्नियन्त्रणाम् ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: But His hymn of Caṇḍikā — that He made secret; and of the merit there is no ending — know that restraint exactly as it is. (Verse 6.) Combined with the commentaries: then He made this very Saptashatī hymn of Caṇḍikā top-secret — making the second path (praise alone) the essence, over the first path (mantra-chanting). So Mārkaṇḍeya told the old tale from the Tantras; then, teaching disciples the Saptashatī's glory, he tells Śiva's intent: the fruit born of reading this hymn never ends, ever — while mantra-chanting-born merit does end. So know exactly as it is that restraint (niyantraṇā) which Śiva built — the narrowing of the first path. One book reads 'they succeed' (sidhyanti) here. The Hindi repeats: Mahādeva made this Saptashatī hymn of Caṇḍikā secret — because other mantras' chant-born merit fades with time, while Saptashatī-reading-born merit never fades. (Continued next.)

passages.mula:
भगवान् शिव ने अन्य मन्त्रों की अपेक्षा जो सप्तशती की ही श्रेष्ठता का निर्णय
किया, उसे यथार्थ ही जानना चाहिए ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: So know as exact truth Śiva's decision preferring Saptashatī over all other mantras. (Verse 6, Hindi completion.) In simple words: God Himself ranked this hymn first — believe it exactly as told.

passages.mula:
सोऽपि क्षेममवाप्नोति सर्वमेव न संशयः ।
कृष्णायां वा चतुर्दश्यामष्टम्यां वा समाहितः ॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: He too attains all welfare, no doubt — on the dark fourteenth or the eighth, composed. (Verse 7.) Combined with Guptavatī: don't think the hymn's power is lost altogether by the lock. To one who learns the unbolting method from the guru's mouth and practises exactly so, success comes as before, needing no other lore at all — then He shows that very method: 'on the dark (fourteenth)' means in whichever month fresh earnings come, in that month — supply the rest. (Continued in Pradīpa.)

passages.mula:
सिद्धिसम्भवादित्याह। सोऽपीति । तमुपायमेव प्रदर्शयति। कृष्णायामिति ।
यस्मिन्मासि नूतनार्जनं तस्मिन्मास इति शेषः ॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: The unbolting method is then shown: on the dark fourteenth or eighth of the month of fresh earnings. (Verse 7, Guptavatī completion.) In simple words: the lock has a key — learn it from the teacher, use it on the dark 14th or 8th, and the old full power returns.

passages.mula:
न तु तद्विना फलमेतस्य नास्तीति एतद्विना तु तत्तन्मन्त्राणां फलमेव न भवतीति
विशेषः ।।७।।
passages.primaryEn: Even the other-mantra chanter, if he joins this hymn's chanting, attains all welfare — so everyone should honour Saptashatī-reading above all. This also teaches: other mantras must be chanted only after reading Saptashatī, or their fruit won't come — because this hymn alone destroys whatever blocks all mantra success, which is why it was first called the un-bolter. 'Un-bolter' means the fault-form that dams success; destroying it, the hymn earns the same name by pointer-sense.
