कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नमः । ॐ ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं चामुण्डायै विच्चे करतलकरपृष्ठाभ्यां
नमः ।
हृदयादिन्यासः
ॐ ऐं हृदयाय नमः । ॐ ह्रीं शिरसे स्वाहा। ॐ क्लीं शिखायै
वषट्। ॐ चामुण्डायै कवचाय हुम्। ॐ विच्चे नेत्रत्रयाय वौषट्। ॐ ऐं
ह्रीं क्लीं चामुण्डायै विच्चे अस्त्राय फट्।
दुर्गासप्तशती
अक्षरन्यासः

नीलाश्मद्युतिमास्यपाददशकां सेवे महाकालिकां
यामस्तौत्स्वपिते हरौ कमलजो हन्तुं मधु कैटभम् ॥१॥

अक्षत्रक्परशुं गदेषुकुलिशं पद्म धनुः कुण्डिकां
दण्डं शक्तिमसिं च चर्म जलजं घण्टां सुराभाजनम् ।
शूलं पाशसुदर्शने च दधतीं हस्तैः प्रसन्नाननां
सेवे सैरिभमर्दिनीमिहं महालक्ष्मी सरोजस्थिताम् ॥२॥

गौरीदेहसमुद्भवां त्रिजगतामाधारभूतां महा-
पूर्वामत्र सरस्वतीमनुभजे शुम्भादिदैत्यार्दिनीम् ॥३॥

इस प्रकार न्यास और ध्यान करके मानसिक उपचार से देवी की पूजा
करे। फिर १०८ बार नवार्णमन्त्र का जप करना चाहिये। जप आरम्भ करने के
पहले 'ऐं ह्रीं अक्षमालिकायै नमः' इस मन्त्र से माला की पूजा करके इस
प्रकार प्रार्थना करें-
* विनियोग न्यास वाक्य तथा ध्यान सम्बन्धी श्लोकों के अर्थ पहले दिये जा चुके हैं।
ॐ मां माले महामाये सर्वशक्तिस्वरूपिणि ।
चतुर्वर्गस्त्वयि न्यस्तस्तस्मान्मे सिद्धिदा भव ।।
ॐ अविघ्नं कुरु माले त्वं गृह्णामि दक्षिणे करे ।
जपकाले च सिद्धयर्थ प्रसीद मम सिद्धये ॥
ॐ अक्षमालाधिपतये सुसिद्धिं देहि देहि सर्वमन्त्रार्थसाधिनि साधय
साधय सर्वसिद्धिं परिकल्पय परिकल्पय मे स्वाहा।
इस प्रकार प्रार्थना करके जप आरम्भ करें। जप पूरा करके उसे भगवती
को समर्पित करते हुए कहें-
गुह्यातिगुह्यगोप्त्री त्वं गृहाणास्मत्कृतं जपम् ।
सिद्धिर्भवतु मे देवि ! त्वत्प्रसादान्महेश्वरि ! ॥
तत्पश्चात् फिर नीचे लिखे अनुसार न्यास करें-
करन्यासः
ॐ ह्रीं अङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां नमः । ॐ चं तर्जनीभ्यां नमः । ॐ डिं मध्यमाभ्यां
नमः । ॐ कां अनामिकाभ्यां नमः । ॐ यै कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नमः । ॐ ह्रीं
चण्डिकायै करतलकरपृष्ठाभ्य नमः ।
हृदयादिन्यासः
ॐ खगिनी शूलिनी घोरा गदिनी चक्रिणी तथा ।
शङ्खिनी चापिनी बाणभुशुण्डीपरिघायुधा ॥ हृदयाय नमः
ॐ शूलेन पाहि नो देवि ! पाहि खड्गेन चाम्बिक्रे ! ।
घण्टास्वनेन नः पाहि चापज्यानिःस्वनेन च ॥ शिरसे स्वाहा ।
ॐ प्राच्यां रक्ष प्रतीच्यां च चण्डिके ! रक्ष दक्षिणे ।
भ्रामणेनात्मशूलस्य उत्तरस्यां तथेश्वरि ! ॥ शिखायै वषट् ।
हुम् ।
ॐ सौम्यानि यानि रूपाणि त्रैलोक्ये विचरन्ति ते ।
यानि चात्यर्थघोराणि तै रक्षास्मांस्तथा भुवम् ॥ कवचाय
ॐ खड्गशूलगदादीनि यानि चास्त्राणि तेऽम्बिके ! ।
करपल्लवसङ्गीनि तैरस्मान् रक्ष सर्वतः ॥ नेत्रत्रयाय वौषट्।

ॐ अहं रुद्रेभिर्वसुभिश्चराम्यहमादित्यैरुत विश्वदेवैः ।
अहं मित्रावरुणोभा बिभर्यहमिन्द्राग्नी अहमश्विनोभा ॥१॥

जो सिंह की पीठ पर विराजमान हैं, जिनके मस्तक पर चन्द्रमा का मुकुट
है, जो मरकतमणि के समान कान्तिवाली अपनी चार भुजाओं में शङ्ख, चक्र,

passages.section: ऋग्वेदोक्तं देवीसूक्तम्अहं दधामि द्रविणं हविष्यते सुप्राव्ये यजमानाय सुन्वते ॥२॥
passages.mula:
अहं राष्ट्री संगमनी वसूनां चिकितुषी प्रथमा यज्ञियानाम् ।
तां मा देवा व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा भूरिस्थात्रां भूयविशयन्तीम् ॥३॥

passages.section: ऋग्वेदोक्तं देवीसूक्तम्अहं दधामि द्रविणं हविष्यते सुप्राव्ये यजमानाय सुन्वते ॥२॥
passages.mula:
मया सो अन्नमत्ति यो विपश्यति यः
प्राणिति य ईं शृणोत्युक्तम् ।
अमन्तवो मां त उप क्षियन्ति श्रुधि
श्रुत श्रद्धिवं ते वदामि ॥४॥

passages.section: ऋग्वेदोक्तं देवीसूक्तम्अहं दधामि द्रविणं हविष्यते सुप्राव्ये यजमानाय सुन्वते ॥२॥
passages.mula:
अहमेव स्वयमिदं वदामि जुष्टं देवेभिरुत मानुषेभिः ।
यं कामये तं तमुग्रं कृणोमि
तं ब्रह्माणं तमृषिं तं सुमेधाम् ॥५॥

अहं रुद्राय धनुरा तनोमि ब्रह्मद्विषे शरवे हन्तवा उ ।
अहं जनाय समदं कृणोम्यहं द्यावापृथिवी आ विवेश ॥६॥

अहं सुवे पितरमस्य मूर्धन्मम
योनिरप्स्वन्तः समुद्रे ।
ततो वि तिष्ठे भुवनानु विश्वो-
तामूं द्यां वर्ष्मणोप स्पृशामि ॥७॥

अहमेव वात इव प्रवाम्यारभमाणा भुवनानि विश्वा ।
परो दिवा पर एना पृथिव्यैतावती महिमा सम्बभूव ॥८॥

मैं ही ब्रह्मद्वेषी हिंसक असुरों का वध करने के लिये रुद्र के धनुष को
चढ़ाती हूँ। मैं ही शरणागतजनों की रक्षा के लिये शत्रुओं से युद्ध करती हूँ

चलती हूँ, स्वेच्छा से ही कर्म में प्रवृत्त होती हूँ। मैं पृथ्वी और आकाश दोनों
से परे हूँ। अपनी महिमा से ही मैं ऐसी हुई हूँ।। ८॥
* इसके बाद तन्त्रोक्त देवीसूक्त दिया गया है, उसका भी पाठ करना चाहिये।

नमो देव्यै महादेव्यै शिवायै सततं नमः ।
नमः प्रकृत्यै भद्रायै नियताः प्रणताः स्म ताम् ॥१॥

कल्याण्यै प्रणतां वृद्धयै सिद्ध्यै कुर्मो नमो नमः ।
नैऋत्यै भूभृतां लक्ष्म्यै शर्वाण्यै ते नमो नमः ॥३॥

दुर्गायै दुर्गपारायै सारायै सर्वकारिण्यै ।
ख्यात्यै तथैव कृष्णायै धूम्रायै सततं नमः ॥४॥

अतिसौम्यातिरौद्रायै नतास्तस्यै नमो नमः ।
नमो जगत्प्रतिष्ठायै देव्यै कृत्यै नमो नमः ॥५॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु क्षुधारूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥१०॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शक्तिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥१२॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु तृष्णारूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥१३॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु जातिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥१५॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु लज्जारूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥१६॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शान्तिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥१७॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु कान्तिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥१९॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु लक्ष्मीरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥२०॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु वृत्तिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥२१॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु स्मृतिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥२२॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु दयारूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥२३॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु तुष्टिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥२४॥

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु मातृरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥२५॥

इन्द्रियाणामधिष्ठात्री भूतानां चाखिलेषु या ।
भूतेषु सततं तस्यै व्याप्तिदेव्यै नमो नमः ॥२७॥

करोतु सा नः शुभहेतुरीश्वरी
शुभानि भद्राण्यभिहन्तु चापदः ॥२९॥

या साम्प्रतं चोद्धतदैत्यतापितै-
रस्माभिरीशा च सुरैर्नमस्यते ।
या च स्मृता तत्क्षणमेव हन्ति नः
सर्वापदो भक्तिविनम्रमूर्तिभिः ॥३०॥

* इसके पश्चात् 'प्राधानिक' आदि तीनों रहस्यों का पाठ करे।
यामलोक्तमन्त्रविभागविचारः
एवं कात्यायनीतन्त्रे प्रतिमन्त्रं विशिष्य विभागो विस्तरेण वर्णितः । यामले
त्वीषत्प्रकारभेदेन चतुःश्लोक्या संक्षिप्य दर्शितः । यथा-
'नवार्णेन हुनेदादौ षोडशाहुतिभिस्तथा ।
चण्ड्येका वैश्य एवैको ब्रह्मको भगवानपि ॥
मार्कण्डेयास्तथा पञ्च राजानो वेदसम्मिताः ।
षड्विंशतिस्तु ऋषयो देव्य एकादश स्मृताः ॥
देवौ द्वावथ दूतौ द्वावध्यायास्तु त्रयोदश ।
श्लोकाः पञ्चशतानि स्युः सप्तपञ्चाशदुत्तराः ।
श्लोकार्धानि चतुश्चत्वारिंशत्संख्यानि निर्दिशेत् ।
सर्वान्ते तु नवार्णेन षोडशाहुतयः पुनः ॥ इति ।
अत्र चण्ड्येका देव्य एकादशेति विभज्य निर्देशेऽपि देवीत्वेनैक्याद्वादश
देव्युक्तय इत्येव द्रष्टव्यम्। केचित्तु विभज्येति बलात्सर्वारम्भे ॐनमश्चण्डिकायै

शतश्लोक्यां सगृहीतः साधैरष्टभिः श्लोकैः ।
यामले तु त्रिपान्मन्त्रः पुनरुक्तश्च नेष्यते ॥७२॥

'वाङ्मन्त्रेषु त्रयं न्यूनमर्धेषु क्रतुबोधिकाः ।
विंशतिः श्लोकसंख्यायामध्याया अपि मन्त्रकाः ॥७३॥

आद्यन्तयोर्नवार्णस्योक्तयः षोडश षोडश ।
एकोऽधिकः श्लोकपिण्डे शेषः सर्वोऽपि पूर्ववत् ॥७४॥

तथा हि प्रथमो वैश्यश्चरमर्षिश्च नादिमे ।
प्रीतौ स्वस्तवयुद्धेनेत्यर्धश्लोकात्मको मनुः ॥७५॥

आवां जहीत्यर्धतः प्राक् पञ्चमे नास्ति देववाक् ।
दशमे जज्वलुश्चेति मनुरर्थोऽधिकोऽन्तिमः ॥७६॥

एवं प्रभावा सा देवी तामुपैहीति पद्ययोः ।
द्वे द्वे अर्धे पृथ‌मन्त्राविति भेदस्त्रयोदशे ॥७७॥

षड्विंशतिश्च ऋषयस्त्रयोदशाध्यायवाक्यानि ।
श्लोकास्तु सप्तपञ्चाशदधिकशतपञ्चकप्रमिताः ॥७९॥

अर्धानि चतुश्चत्वारिंशत्तत्साष्टषट्शतकम् ।
षोडशनवार्णमन्त्रैः पुटितं चेद्यामलोक्तसप्तशती ॥८० ॥

ब्रह्मैको भगवानेको मार्कण्डेयास्तु मार्गणाः ।
दूतवैश्यौ पुनद्वाँ द्वौ राजोवाचेति शाखिनः ॥
देवाः पञ्चर्षयस्त्रिंशद्देव्युवाचेति भास्कराः ।
श्लोकाश्चतुरशीतिस्तु तथा पञ्चशतान्यपि ॥
अर्धानि सप्त च द्वेऽत्र अध्यायास्तु त्रयोदश ।
पदानि पूर्वपदयोस्तथा षोडश षोडश ॥
तानि श्वेताननादीनि सत्यन्तानीति षोडश ।
एते मिलित्वा मन्त्राः स्युः सप्तशत्यभिधानकाः । इति ॥
शाखिनो वेदाश्चत्वारः सप्त च द्वे च नवैवेत्यर्थः । अयमपि पक्षः
शतश्लोक्या निष्कृष्य पञ्चदशभिः श्लोकैः सह्योक्तः ।।

एकोनत्रिंशदूनानि मन्त्रार्थेष्वथ वाङ्मनौ ।
पञ्चाधिकाः सप्तचत्वारिंशत् श्लोकमनुष्वपि ।
आद्यन्तयोर्वैकृतिकरहस्यं पठितं द्विशः ॥
श्वेताननादिसत्यन्तनामषोडशकं पठेत् ।
सार्धा दशश्लोकाः पिण्डेऽध्यायमन्त्रादि पूर्ववत् ॥
प्रकृतितो द्वौ षषष्टिरूनत्रिंशच्चेति मिलित्वा सप्तनवतिर्मन्त्रा न्यूनाः ।
तत्प्रयुक्ता द्वाविंशतिः सार्धचतुर्दश चेति श्लोका लब्धाः सार्धदशश्लोका अप्राकृता

इत्थं त्रयोदशाध्यायेऽप्यर्धमन्त्रा नवैव हि।
श्लोक (बद्ध) षट्कं यथासम्प्रदायमन्विष्य निक्षिपेत् ॥६३॥

चतुर्थाध्याये त्रियतामित्यर्धस्योत्तरम्-
'ददाम्यहमतिप्रीत्या स्तवैरेभिः सुपूजिता ।
कर्तव्यमपरं यच्च दुष्कृतं तन्निवेद्यताम्' ॥
इत्येकः श्लोकः । पञ्चमे लक्ष्मीरूपेणेत्यस्योत्तरं धृतिरूपेणेति
तुष्टिरूपेणेत्यस्योत्तरं पुष्टिरूपेणेति च द्वौ श्लोकौ । एकादशे-
'सर्वतः पाणिपादान्ते! सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखे !।
सर्वतः श्रवणघ्राणे ! नारायणि ! नमोऽस्तु ते' ॥

'विधिभगवन्तौ दूतविशौ देवमृकण्डुजौ शशिद्विशराः ।
नृपदेवर्षयोऽब्ध्यर्कत्रिंशत् संख्यास्त्रयोदशाध्यायाः ॥९६॥

श्लोकाः स्युः पञ्चशतानि चतुराशीतिर्नवार्धानि ।
नाम्नां षोडशभिः सम्पुटिता तन्त्रान्तरोक्तसप्तशती' ॥९७॥

आसु तु तिसृषु प्रथमा प्राच्योदीच्यप्रतीच्यसूरिमता ।
दक्षिणदेश्यैरन्ये आदृतदेश्ये विलुप्तदेश्ये च ॥९८॥

एवं वाक्यं मन्त्रोऽध्याहृत्यानुषक्तिभिः सुयोज्यापि ।
न पुनर्मन्त्रान्तरगतपदसाकाङ्क्षो विना वचनम् ॥९९॥

इति मत्त्वैष परिश्रम इह रचितो मन्त्रलक्षणानुसृतः ।
तदिमं विज्ञाय ज्ञा अज्ञाकलितं विभागमुज्झन्तु ॥१००॥

इति मन्त्रपरिच्छेदो भास्करसंख्यावदात्मनैव कृतः ।
देव्युक्तपरिच्छेदे भास्करसंख्यावदात्मनैव यतः ॥१०१॥

चण्डिस्तवविभागांशे बालोंऽप्युत्कण्ठितो यदि ।
स्यादनेन निबन्धेन शतश्लोकेन पण्डितः ॥ १०२॥

इति श्रीधीरगम्भीररायसोमसुतः सुतः ।
भारत्यधाच्छतश्लोकीं काशीस्थो बचोऽग्निचित् ॥ १०३॥
आदृतदेश्ये इत्यनयोरीषदपरिसमाप्तौ प्रत्ययः । विलुप्तदेश्ये किञ्चिदूनो

प्राधानिकरहस्यम्
कवच, अर्गला, कीलक तथा तीनों रहस्य ये ६ सप्तशती के अङ्ग माने
गये हैं। इसीलिये सप्तशती पाठ के साथ उसके अङ्गभूत कवच, अर्गला, कीलक
तथा तीनों रहस्यों का पाठ भी आवश्यक माना जाता है। क्योंकि अङ्ग के बिना
अङ्गी पूर्ण नहीं होता। कात्यायनी तन्त्र के अधोलिखित श्लोक इसमें प्रमाण हैं-
अङ्गहीनो यथा देही सर्वकर्मसु नाक्षमः ।
अङ्गषट्‌कविहीना तु तथा सप्तशतीस्तुतिः ॥
तस्मादेतत्पठित्वैव जपेत्सप्तशतीं पराम् ।
अन्यथा शापमाप्नोति हानिं चैव पदे पदे ॥
रावणाद्याः स्तोत्रमेतदङ्गहीनं निषेविरे ।
हता रामेण ते यस्मान्नाङ्गहीनं पठेत्ततः ॥
इन ६ अङ्गों में कवच, अर्गला तथा कीलक को सप्तशती पाठ के पूर्व
में तथा रहस्यत्रय को सप्तशती पाठ के अन्त में पढ़ने की प्राचीन काल से
ही सुरक्षित चली आ रही परम्परा आज भी उसी क्रम में विद्यमान है। षडङ्ग
सप्तशती के कवच, अर्गला तथा कीलक इन तीन अङ्गों का विवेचन यथा स्थान
पूर्व में किया जा चुका है। अवशिष्ट रहस्यत्रयरूप तीन अङ्गों में यह प्राधानिक
रहस्य प्रथम तथा षडङ्गों में (इसका स्थान) चौथा है।
अस्य श्रीरहस्यत्रयस्य ब्रह्माऽच्युतरुद्रा ऋषयः । नवदुर्गा देवता । अनुष्टुप्
छन्दः । महालक्ष्मीर्बीजम्। श्रीः शक्तिः । अभीप्सितफलसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे
विनियोगः ।
राजोवाच
भगवन्नवतारा मे चण्डिकायास्त्वयोदिताः ।
एतेषां प्रकृतिं ब्रह्मन् प्रधानं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥१॥

जो स्वरूप जिस विधि से मेरे द्वारा आराध्य है' उसे आप सम्पूर्ण रूप से
भलीभाँति प्रणत मुझसे अर्थात् आपके चरणों में पड़े हुए मुझसे कहिये ।। १॥२॥
passages.primaryEn: The king asks with folded hands: tell me fully — what is Her true form, and in what way should I worship Her? (Verses 1–2, Hindi.) In simple words Suratha the king begs the sage: show me exactly who the Mother is and how I should serve Her — hold nothing back from surrendered me.

passages.mula:
ऋषिरुवाच
इदं रहस्यं परममनाख्येयं प्रचक्षते ।
भक्तोऽसीति न मे किञ्चित्तवावाच्यं नराधिप ॥३॥
passages.primaryEn: The sage speaks: this mystery is supreme, not fit to be told — yet since you are a devotee, O king among men, nothing of mine is untellable to you. (Verse 3.) Combined with Guptavatī's opening key to the whole mystery: 'you are a devotee' means devotee of both Goddess and guru. At the book's start the truth-form was told — Brahman as religion itself, named by the word Caṇḍikā, the worshipped reality — and its three branch-forms: Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī, Mahāsarasvatī. So Caṇḍikā the fourth is the Whole itself, religion-shaped, beyond qualities — yet counted fifth. Since telling the three branches nearly tells their undivided Whole, the fourth, the text wordlessly drops the Whole and points instead to one of the branches as equal to the fourth in shelter-giving — calling it three-qualitied, formless, unseeable, dwelling within the three descents. (Continued next.)

passages.mula:
सगुणातुर्यामपहृत्य त्रयान्यतमात एवेतरे द्वे निःसृते इत्यादिरीत्या सृष्टिं
कथयितुमारभते ।। ३ ।।
passages.primaryEn: Taking the pure-goodness Whole aside from the three, the text begins telling creation from one of the three alone — how from it the other two streamed out. (Verse 3, Guptavatī completion.) In simple words the method is shown: keep the fourth (the Whole) quietly aside, and tell the whole creation-story through Mahālakṣmī, from whom the other two goddesses flow.

passages.mula:
कहते हैं, परन्तु यतः आप भक्त हैं, इसलिये आपसे न कहने योग्य कुछ भी
मेरे पास नहीं है।। ३॥
passages.primaryEn: The sage said to the king: this mystery, asked by you, is top-secret — worth telling only in secret. But since you are a devotee, nothing is untellable to me for you. (Verse 3, Hindi.) In simple words the teacher tests and then trusts: this wisdom is too precious for casual ears, but a true devotee may hear everything.

passages.mula:
सर्वस्याद्या महालक्ष्मीस्त्रिगुणा परमेश्वरी ।
लक्ष्यालक्ष्यस्वरूपा सा व्याप्य कृत्स्नं व्यवस्थिता
passages.primaryEn: Mahālakṣmī, first of all, three-qualitied, supreme Lady — of seen-and-unseen form, She stands pervading everything. (Verse 4.) Combined with the commentaries: 'first of all' — the three-qualitied Whole of goodness-passion-darkness faces is itself the first cause of the whole expanse, say some; others say Mahālakṣmī here is not one of the three branches but another name of the fourth, Caṇḍikā Herself — 'Śivā named Śakti, seated on Sadāśiva's lap, famed as Mahālakṣmī, rich in all gods' qualities,' says the Śiva Purāṇa. Not so, answers Guptavatī: the Mahālakṣmī inside the sacrifices stands apart, being passion-heavy, praised through ten names, with no telling of the other two — so supplying extra words just to force that reading is painful twisting. 'Seen' means with qualities, 'unseen' means without qualities — Her grasping never shows, so She is called unseen; as the Goddess-Atharva-Top scripture says, She is knowledge whose object is Herself — knowledge that kills mere mind-knowledge. For 'I know this pot' ends in 'I', and though Brahman is reached by the last mind-wave, It is never reached as a fruit-object — that is the feeling. One book reads 'and twice-born' here.

passages.mula:
स्वाविषयकेति तेषां घटमहं जानामीत्येवकारात्, ब्रह्मणश्चरमवृत्तिव्याप्यत्वेऽपि
फलव्याप्यत्वानङ्गीकारादिति भावः ॥४॥
passages.primaryEn: Knowledge whose object is Herself — never grasped as a fruit-object, though the last mind-wave touches It. (Verse 4, Guptavatī completion.) In simple words the deepest point: you cannot 'know' the Mother the way you know a pot — She is the knowing itself, not a thing to be known.

passages.mula:
ही हैं। लक्ष्या लक्ष्यस्वरूपा अर्थात् दृश्य और अदृश्य रूप से वे ही सम्पूर्ण
ब्रह्माण्ड को व्याप्त करके स्थित हैं।।४।।
passages.primaryEn: The three-qualitied supreme Lady Mahālakṣmī, first of all, stands pervading the whole universe in seen and unseen form. (Verse 4, Hindi.) In simple words: before everything, the three-powered great Goddess — visible as the world, invisible as its soul — fills all.

passages.mula:
मातुलिङ्गं गदां खेटं पानपात्रं च बिभ्रती ।
नागं लिङ्गं च योनिं च बिभ्रती नृप मूर्धनि ॥५॥
passages.primaryEn: Citron, mace, shield and drinking-cup She holds; serpent, emblem and womb-sign She wears, O king, on the crown. (Verse 5.) In simple words the Mother's four hands hold citron-fruit, mace, shield and wine-cup, while Her crown mysteriously carries serpent, Śiva-mark and Goddess-mark.

passages.mula:
तप्तकाञ्चनवर्णाभा तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणा ।
शून्यं तदखिलं स्वेन पूरयामास तेजसा ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: Glowing like heated gold, decked in heated-gold ornaments — She filled all that emptiness with Her own glory. (Verse 6.) In simple words: golden-bodied, gold-decked, She poured Her own light into the total void until nothing empty remained.

passages.mula:
शून्यं तदखिलं लोकं विलोक्य परमेश्वरी ।
बभार रूपमपरं तमसा केवलेन हि ॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: Seeing all that world empty, the supreme Lady wore another form — of mere darkness only. (Verse 7.) In simple words: looking at the hollow universe, out of Her own dark side She put on a second body.

passages.mula:
सा भिन्नाञ्जनसङ्काशा दंष्ट्राञ्जितवरानना ।
विशाललोचना नारी बभूव तनुमध्यमा ॥८॥
passages.primaryEn: She became a woman — smooth-dark like collyrium, with fangs lighting Her noble face, wide-eyed, slim-waisted. (Verse 8.) Combined with the commentaries: pointing to the 'seen' — citron means the seed-filled fruit; 'shield' is hide, held in hands, supply that; serpent and the other two She wears on the crown — 'emblem' here is Rudra's male mark, 'womb' Viṣṇu's female mark (for the Veda bids 'fashion a Viṣṇu-womb'), so by leftover logic the serpent must be Brahmā's mark. Thus She shows Herself as Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra in one, male-female in one. Then the 'unseen': at world-dissolution the world rests as seed-habit without gross form — that She pervaded with Her glory, which is pure consciousness, is the sense. And that same Mahālakṣmī ripened further into Mahākālī-hood — 'seeing emptiness' (verses 7–8). The Hindi prayer repeats: O king, four-armed Mahālakṣmī holds citron (sweet-lime fruit), mace, shield and wine-cup, and wears serpent, emblem and womb-marks on the head (5); glowing like heated gold, wearing heated-gold ornaments (continued next).

passages.mula:
की आभा वाली हैं, तथा तपाये हुए स्वर्ण की कान्ति वाले आभूषणों को धारण
करने वाली हैं। अपने तेज से उन्होंने सम्पूर्ण शून्य को पूरित किया है ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: Glowing like heated gold, wearing heated-gold ornaments, She filled the whole void with Her glory. (Verse 6, Hindi.) In simple words the golden Mother floods the emptiness with light until it shines.

passages.mula: निश्चय ही उस परमेश्वरी ने उस सम्पूर्ण लोक को शून्य देखकर इसी कारण केवल
passages.primaryEn: Seeing the whole world hollow, the supreme Lady surely wore a second form from Her dark side only. (Verse 7, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: from Mahālakṣmī's dark share was born that woman — smooth like collyrium, with out-jutting splitter fangs lighting Her noble face, wide-eyed and slim-bodied. (Verse 8.)

passages.mula:
खड्गपात्रशिरःखेटेरलङ्कृतचतुर्भुजा
कबन्धहारं शिरसा बिभ्राणा शिरसां स्त्रजम् ॥९॥
passages.primaryEn: Sword, wine-cup, head and shield-decked, four-armed; wearing a trunk-garland on the chest, a head-garland on the head. (Verse 9.) In simple words the dark Mother's four arms glitter — sword, cup, severed head, shield — with headless trunks garlanding Her chest and a skull-garland on Her head.

passages.mula:
तां प्रोवाच महालक्ष्मीस्तामसीं प्रमदोत्तमाम् ।
ददामि तव नामानि यानि कर्माणि तानि ते ॥१०॥
passages.primaryEn: To Her, finest of proud ladies, Mahālakṣmī spoke: I give you the names — and yours shall be the deeds. (Verse 10.) In simple words the golden Mother addresses the newly-born dark lady, best of women: I shall give you names, and matching works shall be yours.

passages.mula:
महामाया महाकाली महामारी क्षुधा तृषा ।
निद्रा तृष्णा चैकवीरा कालरात्रिर्दुरत्यया ॥११॥
passages.primaryEn: Mahāmāyā, Mahākālī, Mahāmārī, hunger, thirst; sleep, craving, the One Heroine, Night-of-death hard to cross. (Verse 11.) Combined with the commentaries: 'head' means the neck-part set on a pole, the skull-staff; 'trunks' are headless bodies — supply 'on the chest'; She wears a trunk-garland on the chest and a head-garland on the head, is the sense. 'To Her spoke' — but some read the first and second persons swapped, making it the dark lady's sentence — wasted effort, that. For the उत्तर-half 'give me name and deed, O Mother, salutation to You' is seen in many books — which rather unjoins it; so some people's case-split reading too is not to be taken. With no question from the goodness-natured one, the name-first answer ahead tells it. (Verses 9–11.) The Hindi prayer repeats: four arms graced with sword, wine-cup, head and shield; trunk-garland on the chest, skull-garland on the head (9). Some books add here an extra verse — the dark finest lady asks Mahālakṣmī: 'give me name and deed, O Mother, salutation to You' — but since most books don't agree, it ranks as inserted. Then Mahālakṣmī to the newly-born finest dark lady: 'I am giving you your names and telling your deeds' (10): Mahāmāyā, Mahākālī, Mahāmārī, hunger, thirst, sleep, craving, One Heroine, death-night and hard-to-cross (11). One book reads 'wearing a head-garland indeed' here.

passages.mula:
इमानि तव नामानि प्रतिपाद्यानि कर्मभिः ।
एभिः कर्माणि ते ज्ञात्वा योऽधीते सोऽश्नुते सुखम् ॥१२॥
passages.primaryEn: These are your names, to be proved by your deeds; knowing your deeds through them, whoever studies gains joy. (Verse 12.) In simple words: live these ten names through Your works, and whoever learns Your deeds through them and sings them will taste happiness.

passages.mula:
तामित्युक्त्वा महालक्ष्मीः स्वरूपमपरं नृप ।
सत्त्वाख्येनातिशुद्धेन गुणेनेन्दुप्रभं दधौ ॥१३॥
passages.primaryEn: Having thus spoken to Her, Mahālakṣmī, O king, wore another form — by the over-pure quality called goodness, moon-bright. (Verse 13.) In simple words: after naming the dark daughter, Mahālakṣmī Herself put on a second body of purest goodness, glowing like moonlight.

passages.mula:
अक्षमालाङ्कशधरा वीणापुस्तकधारिणी ।
सा बभूव वरा नारी नामान्यस्यै च सा ददौ ॥१४॥
passages.primaryEn: Rosary, goad and lute-book-bearer, She became a lovely woman — and to Her too She gave names. (Verse 14.) Combined with Guptavatī's ten-name soul-meanings from the Kālī Purāṇa (Mahāmāyā: She who keeps the womb-wise being pushed by birth-winds, born wisdom-less, ever yoking him through past-life habits — into delusion, mine-ness, doubt at day's start, then hurling him again and again into anger, checks, greed, then joining him to lust, worry night and day, joylessness and vice-addiction — hence the world-Queen is hailed Great Illusion; and the Devī Purāṇa's name-meaning chapter gives the other names — seek them there). Name-chanting with such meaning-knowledge beforehand is what bears fruit. 'Through them' (verse 12). And that She ripened into Mahāsarasvatī-hood too: 'having spoken to Her' — and the verse 'these are yours' joins to that ten-name set as well. (Verses 13–14.) The Hindi prayer repeats: these ten are your names, to prove true through your deeds in days to come; whoever learns your deeds through them, sings and reflects, will enjoy joy (12). O king, telling the dark Goddess so, Mahālakṣmī wore by purest goodness a second moon-bright form (13). That finest lady held rosary, goad, lute and book in hand — and Mahālakṣmī gave names to Her too (14).

passages.mula:
नापि सैव परिणतेत्याह । तामिति। इमानि तवेति श्लोक एतनामदशकेऽपि
योज्यः ।।१३ ।।१४॥
passages.primaryEn: The same ten-name verse joins here too, and the moon-bright second form follows. (Verses 13–14, Guptavatī seal.) In simple words: the name-giving pattern repeats for the bright daughter exactly as for the dark one.

passages.mula:
में) अक्षमाला, अङ्कुश, बीणा तथा पुस्तक धारण किये हुए थी और उन
महालक्ष्मी ने इस नारी के लिये भी नामों को दिया।। १४॥
passages.primaryEn: Rosary, goad, lute and book in hand — and Mahālakṣmī gave names to this lady too. (Verse 14, Hindi.) In simple words the bright daughter rises holding prayer-beads, elephant-goad, music and scripture — and receives Her own ten names.

passages.mula:
महाविद्या महावाणी भारती वाक् सरस्वती ।
आर्या ब्राह्मी महाधेनुर्वेदगर्भा सुरेश्वरी ॥१५॥
passages.primaryEn: Mahāvidyā, Mahāvāṇī, Bhāratī, Vāk, Sarasvatī; Āryā, Brāhmī, Mahādhenu, Vedagarbhā, Sureśvarī. (Verse 15.) In simple words the ten names of the bright daughter: Great Wisdom, Great Speech, Eloquence, Voice, Flowing One, Noble Lady, Creator's Power, Great Milk-Cow, Veda-Womb, Queen of gods.

passages.mula:
अथोवाच महालक्ष्मीर्महाकालीं सरस्वतीम् ।
युवां जनयतां देव्यौ मिथुने स्वानुरूपतः ॥१६॥
passages.primaryEn: Then Mahālakṣmī said to Mahākālī and Sarasvatī: bring forth, O goddesses, a pair each, after your own likeness. (Verse 16.) In simple words the golden Mother commands Her two daughters: each of you create one woman-and-man pair in your own image.

passages.mula:
इत्युक्त्वा ते महालक्ष्मीः ससर्ज मिथुनं स्वयम् ।
हिरण्यगर्भों रुचिरौ स्त्रीपुंसौ कमलासनौ ॥१७॥
passages.primaryEn: So told, they — Mahālakṣmī Herself created a pair: golden-wombed, lovely, a woman and man on lotus seats. (Verse 17.) In simple words: commanded so, Mahālakṣmī first created a couple Herself — both golden-wombed, beautiful, seated on lotuses, one woman one man.

passages.mula:
ब्रह्मन् विधे विरिञ्चेति धातरित्याह तं नरम् ।
श्रीः पद्म कमले लक्ष्मीत्याह माता स्त्रियं च ताम् ॥१८॥
passages.primaryEn: 'O Brahman! O Maker! O Creator! O Holder!' — She called the man; 'O Fortune! O Lotus! O Lovely! O Luck!' — the mother called the woman. (Verse 18.) In simple words the Mother names Her first children: him — Brahman, Maker, Creator, Holder; her — Fortune, Lotus, Lovely, Luck.

passages.mula:
महाकाली भारती च मिथुने सृजतिस्म ह ।
एतयोरपि रूपाणि नामानि च वदामि ते ॥१९॥
passages.primaryEn: Mahākālī and Bhāratī too created a pair, indeed; their forms and names also I tell you. (Verse 19.) In simple words: the dark and bright daughters each made a couple too — and the sage promises to describe all their faces and names.

passages.mula:
नीलकण्ठं रक्तबाहुं श्वेताङ्गं चन्द्रशेखरम् ।
जनयामास पुरुषं महाकाली सितां स्त्रियम् ॥२०॥
passages.primaryEn: Blue-throated, red-armed, white-limbed, moon-crested — a man Mahākālī bore, and a fair woman. (Verse 20.) Combined with Guptavatī's grammar: 'in a pair a son and a daughter' — a brother-sister twin. 'Herself' here some explain as 'bearing Her own Śrī-named branch-form' — but for us who say Mahālakṣmī is the branch's very name, no such strain. (Verses 15–20.) The Hindi prayer lists: Mahāvidyā 1, Mahāvāṇī 2, Bhāratī 3, Vāk 4 (with variant notes 5 Sarasvatī, 6 Āryā, 7 Brāhmī, 8 wish-cow, 9 Veda-womb, 10 queen of wisdom — 'these ten shall be your names', verse 15). Then Mahālakṣmī bade Mahākālī and Mahāsarasvatī each bring forth a woman-man pair in their own likeness (16). So told, Mahālakṣmī Herself made a pair — both golden-wombed, lovely, lotus-seated (17). Then Mother Mahālakṣmī addressed the man as Brahman, Maker, Creator, Holder, and the woman as Fortune, Lotus, Lovely, Luck (18). Mahākālī and Mahāsarasvatī each made a pair too — 'their faces and names I tell you, Suratha' (19). Mahākālī bore a blue-throated, red-armed, white-limbed, moon-crested man, and with him a fair woman (20).

passages.mula:
केचिद् व्याचक्षते । महालक्ष्मीरिति व्यष्ट्या एव नामेति च वदतामस्माकं तु नायं
क्लेशः ।। १७।। १८ ।। १९।।२० ।।
passages.primaryEn: The pair-grammar settled: son-daughter, brother-sister twins — and Mahālakṣmī needs no strained reading, since the name is Hers by branch-right. (Verses 15–20, Guptavatī seal.) In simple words the commentator refuses twisted grammar: the golden Mother simply is Mahālakṣmī, and the twins are plainly son and daughter.

passages.mula:
वाले तथा मस्तक पर चन्द्रधारण करने वाले एक पुरुष को तथा साथ ही गौरवर्ण
वाली एक स्त्री को उत्पन्न किया।।२०॥
passages.primaryEn: Mahākālī bore a blue-throated, red-armed, white-limbed, moon-crested man, and a fair woman with him. (Verse 20, Hindi.) In simple words the dark daughter's children: a moon-crowned blue-throated son with red arms and white limbs, and a fair daughter beside him.

passages.mula:
सः रुद्रः शङ्करः स्थाणुः कपर्दी च त्रिलोचनः ।
त्रयी विद्या कामधेनुः सा स्त्री भाषाक्षरा स्वरा ॥२१॥
passages.primaryEn: He is Rudra, Śaṅkara, the Still One, the braided, the three-eyed; she is the triple lore, wisdom, wish-cow — speech, letter, note. (Verse 21.) In simple words the twins are named: he — Rudra, Kind-Doer, Stillness, Matted-Locks, Three-Eyes; she — the three Vedas, Learning, Wish-Cow, Language, Letter, Musical Note.

passages.mula:
सरस्वती स्त्रियं गौरीं कृष्णं च पुरुषं नृप ।
जनयामास नामानि तयोरपि वदामि ते ॥२२॥
passages.primaryEn: Sarasvatī bore a fair woman and a dark man, O king — their names too I tell you. (Verse 22.) In simple words the bright daughter's twins: a fair daughter and a dark son — hear their names next.

passages.mula:
विष्णुः कृष्णो हृषीकेषो वासुदेवो जनार्दनः ।
उमा गौरी सती चण्डी सुन्दरी सुभगा शिवा ॥२३॥
passages.primaryEn: Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, Heart-Lord, All-Pervader, Man-Rescuer; Umā, Gaurī, Satī, Caṇḍī, Lovely, Lucky, Blessed. (Verse 23.) In simple words: he is Viṣṇu by five names, she is Umā by seven — the Preserver pair fully named.

passages.mula:
एवं युवतयः सद्यः पुरुषत्वं प्रपेदिरे ।
चक्षुष्मन्तोऽनुपश्यन्ति नेतरेऽतद्विदो जनाः ॥२४॥
passages.primaryEn: Thus the young women at once reached manhood; the eyed ones see it truly — other men, not knowing that, do not. (Verse 24.) Combined with Guptavatī's deep key: 'triple lore and wisdom' — scholarly or not, each is a separate name-pair (verses 21–23). Having made three pairs, since weddings need bride-giving parents and no other men exist but themselves, they themselves took double-form, male-and-female both — 'thus' says so. Manhood Mahālakṣmī reached, Brahmahood Mahākālī, Rudrahood Mahāsarasvatī, Viṣṇuhood — is the sense. For though young women, they hold manhood too — not as two persons, nor half-and-half like the half-woman-lord, but both all-pervading, like sunlight and shade both filling the same bowl of water — that is the feeling. And this form is unseen to flesh-eyes, says 'the eyed': wisdom alone, fed by the teacher's nine-lettered grace, is the true eye — 'not knowing that' reads un-split. (Verse 24.) The Hindi prayer repeats it whole: Rudra-Śaṅkara-Still-Matted-Three-eyed he; triple-lore-wisdom-wish-cow-speech-letter-note she (21); O king, Mahāsarasvatī bore a fair woman and a dark man — hear both their names (22): Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, Heart-Lord, All-Pervader, Man-Rescuer he; Umā, Gaurī, Satī, Caṇḍī, Lovely, Lucky, Blessed she (23). Thus the three maidens at once became men too — the eyed (wisdom-given by the teacher) surely see it; others, not knowing this wisdom, cannot see. (24.)

passages.mula:
रूपं चर्मचक्षुषामदृश्यमित्याह। चक्षुष्मन्त इति। ज्ञानस्यैव चक्षुर्गुणपौष्कल्येन
मुख्यचक्षुष्ट्वं नवार्णस्येति भावः । अतद्विद इति छेदः ॥ २४।।
passages.primaryEn: Three maidens became men too — not as split halves but both-wholly, like light and shade filling one bowl — seen only by wisdom-eyes, not flesh-eyes. (Verse 24, Guptavatī seal.) In simple words the mystery's heart: each goddess is fully woman and fully man at once, and only the teacher-opened eye can see it.

passages.mula:
ब्रह्मणे प्रददौ पत्नी महालक्ष्मीर्नृप त्रयीम् ।
रुद्राय गौरी वरदां वासुदेवाय च श्रियम् ॥२५॥
passages.primaryEn: To Brahmā Mahālakṣmī gave as wife Trayī; to Rudra, boon-giving Gaurī; and Śrī to Vāsudeva. (Verse 25.) In simple words the three weddings: Brahmā weds Learning, Rudra weds Fair Gaurī, Viṣṇu weds Fortune.

passages.mula:
स्वरया सह सम्भूय विरिञ्चोऽण्डमजीजनत् ।
बिभेद भगवान् रुद्रस्तद्‌गौर्या सह वीर्यवान् ॥२६॥
passages.primaryEn: With Svarā joined, Brahmā hatched an egg; potent Rudra split it with Gaurī. (Verse 26.) In simple words: Brahmā with Learning laid the cosmic egg, and mighty Rudra with Fair One broke it open.

passages.mula:
अण्डमध्ये
प्रधानादिकार्यजातमभून्नृप ।
महाभूतात्मकं सर्वं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥२७॥
passages.primaryEn: Inside the egg, O king, came the whole brood from First-cause — the entire still-and-moving world of five-element stuff. (Verse 27.) In simple words: inside that egg unfolded everything — from root nature through ego and elements (the Sāṅkhya list) — the whole moving-and-unmoving universe.

passages.mula:
पुपोष पालयामास तल्लक्ष्म्या सह केशवः ।
महालक्ष्मीरेव मता राजन् सर्वेश्वरेश्वरी ॥२८॥
passages.primaryEn: Keśava with Lakṣmī fed and guarded it; and Mahālakṣmī alone, O king, is held Queen of the lords of all. (Verse 28.) Combined with the commentaries: 'with Svarā joined' means met with triple-lore wisdom; 'that' — the egg-world of root-nature, ego and elements in order, the Sāṅkhya tattva-group (verses 26–27). 'Mahālakṣmī' — both Her formless and formed faces are Hers, not the other two's. So among the three branches, the Mahālakṣmī tinged with passion-chiefly usable two qualities, both-formed-and-formless, is the worshippable — that is the triple group. And to remove the doubt 'why are Mahālakṣmī's ten names barely sung if the branches matter most' — 'She alone' answers: since She alone gives names to the others, endless regress stops at the Giver needing no other giver — that is the 'alone'. The Hindi prayer repeats the weddings and world-making whole: Mahālakṣmī gave Learning to Brahmā, boon-Gaurī to Rudra, Fortune to Vāsudeva (25); with Learning Brahmā laid an egg; potent Rudra with Fair One split it (26); inside, O king, came the root-cause brood — the whole five-element still-moving world (27); then Keśava-Viṣṇu with Lakṣmī fed and guarded it all (and with Fair One the Great Lord later destroyed it all — a verse some books carry but the original here lacks). So, O king, Mahālakṣmī alone stands as Queen of all lords (other books: 'Mahālakṣmī the All-goodness Queen and All-Queen', verse 28).

passages.mula:
निराकारा च सकारा सैव नानाभिधानभृत् ।
नामान्तरैर्निरूप्यैषा नाम्ना नान्येन केनचित् ॥२९॥
passages.primaryEn: She alone is formless and formed, bearing many titles; by other names She is to be known — by no other name but names. (Verse 29.) In simple words the seal-verse: formless and formed both, many-named, She is known through names alone — and through no name but names.

passages.mula: इति प्रधानिकरहस्यम्।
passages.primaryEn: Thus ends the Prādhāna mystery. Combined with Guptavatī's grand finale: 'by other names' means by the other two branches' names alone — since the Fourth needs no separate names of Her own, that is the feeling. So with the Fourth quietly set aside, the Mahālakṣmī inside the three branches is the very best — that devotee-pride is the book's own natural intent. Hence the Saptashatī's four hymns: the Goddess-hymn praises the Fourth through the non-difference of Mahākālī and the other two; the other three hymns serve the three quality-faces in turn — that is the fine point. Others say the Fourth alone is worshippable and all three branches are low, and they painfully drag this book to say: Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī, Mahāsarasvatī rule the three stories in turn, and the Fourth rules only the nine-lettered — but if the Saptashatī worshipped branches alone and never the Fourth, then the Lakṣmī-Tantra's Indra-dialogue (where ten descents are told from Mahālakṣmī first through Mahākālī to Bhrāmarī, closing with 'supreme is She, firm-set, greatly blest Mahālakṣmī, nature, supreme Lady; for Her praise Brahmā and all gods saw the Goddess-hymn, giver of all wished fruits; chanting it daily, crossing all pains, one wins great lordship; and Her descents with stories Vasiṣṭha told of old to King Suratha of the Svārociṣa age and to the surrendered merchant Samādhi') — all that would clash. For it proves the branch-dwelling Mahālakṣmī's firmness, Her non-difference, the Goddess-hymn's devotion to Her alone, and the three stories' devotion to Her through the branches — clarified by the Fourth Herself. So the whole Saptashatī is Mahālakṣmī wearing non-difference with the Fourth as supreme — which is why 'by one, or by the middle' allows the middle story alone as option for all three stories together — that is the direction. (Verse 29, end of Guptavatī on the Prādhāna mystery.) The Hindi prayer repeats: Mahālakṣmī alone is formless and formed, bearing many names — so She is knowable through those name-forms, and through no single other name. (29.)

passages.mula:
के द्वारा अर्थात् उन सभी नामों के द्वारा निरूप्य हैं अर्थात् इनका निरूपण उन
सभी नामान्तरों से हो सकता है, किसी एक अन्य नाम से नहीं।। २९॥
passages.primaryEn: Through those very name-forms She is knowable — through no other single name. (Verse 29, Hindi.) In simple words the closing seal: don't hunt for one magic word — know Her through all Her names together.

passages.mula:
वैकृतिकरहस्यम्
ऋषिरुवाच
त्रिगुणा तामसी देवी सात्त्विकी या त्रिधोदिता ।
सा शर्वा चण्डिका दुर्गा भद्रा भगवतीर्यते ॥ १ ॥
passages.primaryEn: The sage speaks: the Goddess told as threefold — three-qualitied, dark-natured, goodness-natured — She is called Śarvā, Caṇḍikā, Durgā, Bhadrā, Bhagavatī. (Vaikṛta verse 1.) In simple words the mystery of Her changed (vaikṛta) faces opens: one Mother, three natures — passion-full Mahālakṣmī, dark Mahākālī, bright Mahāsarasvatī — and by five more names She is hailed: with-Śarva, Fierce One, Hard-to-reach, Blessed, Fortuned.

passages.mula:
योगनिद्रा हरेरुक्ता महाकाली तमोगुणा ।
मधुकैटभनाशार्थं यां तुष्टावाम्बुजासनः ॥२॥
passages.primaryEn: Hari's sleep-yoga, they say, is Mahākālī of dark quality — whom lotus-seated Brahmā praised to kill Madhu-Kaiṭabha. (Verse 2.) In simple words: the sleep that closed Viṣṇu's eyes at world-start is Herself — dark Mahākālī, praised by Brahmā on His lotus when the two demons came to kill Him.

passages.mula:
दशवक्त्रा दशभुजा दशपादाञ्जनप्रभा ।
विशालया राजमाना त्रिंशल्लोचनमालया ॥३॥
passages.primaryEn: Ten-faced, ten-armed, ten-footed, glowing like collyrium; shining with a vast thirty-eye garland. (Verse 3.) In simple words the dark Mother's awesome arithmetic: ten faces, ten arms, ten feet, kohl-black shine, and thirty wide eyes strung like a garland.

passages.mula:
स्फुरद्दशनदंष्ट्राभा भीमरूपापि भूमिप ।
रूपसौभाग्यकान्तीनां सा प्रतिष्ठा महाश्रियाम् ॥४॥
passages.primaryEn: Though of terrible form, O king — glittering teeth and fangs — She is the home of beauty, luck, glow and great fortunes. (Verse 4.) In simple words: yes, She looks fearsome with flashing fangs — yet that very form is where beauty, fortune, radiance and all riches live.

passages.mula:
खड्गबाणगदाशूलशङ्खचक्रभुशुण्डिभृत्
परिघं कार्मुकं शीर्ष निश्चोतद्रुधिरं दधौ ॥५॥
passages.primaryEn: Bearing sword, arrow, mace, spear, conch, discus, sling — mace-staff, bow, and a head dripping blood She held. (Verse 5.) In simple words Her ten hands hold ten weapons: sword, arrow, mace, spear, conch, discus, fire-sling, iron club, bow — and a dripping severed head.

passages.mula:
एषा सा वैष्णवी माया महाकाली दुरत्यया ।
आराधिता वशीकुर्यात्पूजाकर्तुश्चराचरम् ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: She is Viṣṇu's illusion, Mahākālī hard to cross; worshipped, She brings the moving world under the worshipper's sway. (Verse 6.) Combined with the commentaries: 'three-qualitied' means passion-chief with darkness-goodness as side-shades. 'With-Śarva' takes no feminine ending for lack of husband-sense. (Verse 1.) Then Mahākālī's other form: 'sleep-yoga' (2); three eyes per face is meant by 'thirty' (3–4); weapons in order from low-right hand to low-left: sword and the rest, 'head' is the skull-staff (5–6). The Hindi prayer repeats it whole: three-named Goddess — passion-Mahālakṣmī, dark-Mahākālī, bright-Mahāsarasvatī — hailed as Śarvā, Caṇḍikā, Durgā, Bhadrā, Bhagavatī (1); dark Mahākālī, Viṣṇu's sleep, praised by lotus-Brahmā against Madhu-Kaiṭabha (2); kohl-glow, ten faces, ten arms, ten feet, thirty-eye garland (3); O king, though terrible with glittering teeth-fangs, home of beauty, luck, glow and great fortunes (4); sword 1, arrow 2, mace 3, spear 4, conch 5 (with variants: discus 6, sling 7, and club 8, bow 9, and the ever-bleeding severed head 10 — held in ten hands) (5); this Viṣṇu-illusion Mahākālī, though unconquerable, worshipped, lays the moving world at the worshipper's feet (6).

passages.mula:
सर्वदेवशरीरेभ्यो याविर्भूतामितप्रभा ।
त्रिगुणा सा महालक्ष्मीः साक्षान्महिषमर्दिनी ॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: From all the gods' bodies burst boundless-glory She — three-qualitied Mahālakṣmī Herself, the Buffalo-killer. (Verse 7.) In simple words the middle story's Queen steps out: born from every god's body-fire fused in one, endless in glory — Mahālakṣmī the three-powered, slayer of Mahiṣa in person.

passages.mula:
श्वेतानना नीलभुजा सुश्वेतस्तनमण्डला ।
रक्तमध्या
सुचित्रजघना
रक्तपादा नीलजङ्गोरुरुन्मदा ॥८॥
passages.primaryEn: White-faced, blue-armed, snowy-breasted, red-waisted; fair-footed, blue-thighed, proudly mad. (Verse 8.) In simple words Her strange beauty is painted limb by limb: white face, blue arms, snow-white breasts, red middle, red feet, blue thighs — drunk with unconquered pride.

passages.mula:
चित्रमाल्याम्बरविभूषणा
चित्रानुलेपना का रूपसौभाग्यशालिनी ॥९॥
passages.primaryEn: Decked in bright garlands, robes and paints — beauty-luck-rich in form. (Verse 9.) In simple words: many-colored garlands, clothes and body-paints — radiance, beauty and fortune all in one body.

passages.mula:
अष्टादशभुजा पूज्या सा सहस्रभुजा सती ।
आयुधान्यत्र वक्ष्यन्ते दक्षिणाधः करक्रमात् ॥१०॥
passages.primaryEn: Eighteen-armed, worshipful — though thousand-armed in truth. Her weapons now are told, from low-right hand in order. (Verse 10.) In simple words: for worship count eighteen arms (though really She has a thousand) — and here comes the weapon-list, starting low-right, hand by hand.

passages.mula:
अक्षमाला च कमलं बाणोऽसिः कुलिशं गदा ।
चक्रं त्रिशूलं परशुः शङ्को घण्टा च पाशकः ॥११॥
passages.primaryEn: Rosary and lotus, arrow and sword, thunderbolt and mace; discus, trident, axe, conch, bell and noose. (Verse 11, first twelve.) In simple words the first twelve in order: beads, lotus, arrow, sword, thunderbolt, mace, discus, trident, axe, conch, bell, noose.

passages.mula:
शक्तिर्दण्डश्चर्म चाप पानपात्रं कमण्डलुः ।
अलङ्कृतभुजामेभिरायुधैः कमलासनाम् ॥१२॥
passages.primaryEn: Spear and staff, hide and bow, wine-cup and water-pot — with these weapons Her arms are graced, lotus-seated. (Verse 12, last six.) In simple words the last six: spear, staff, shield, bow, cup, flask — eighteen arms all weapon-bright, seated on a lotus.

passages.mula:
सर्वदेवमयीमीशां महालक्ष्मीमिमां नृप ! ।
पूजयेत्सर्वदेवानां स लोकानां प्रभुर्भवेत् ॥१३॥
passages.primaryEn: This Mahālakṣmī, made of all gods, the Lady — O king, whoever worships Her becomes lord of worlds and gods. (Verse 13.) Combined with the commentaries: then Mahālakṣmī's changed form: 'from all gods' (verses 7–9); 'thousand-armed' really means endless-armed (10–13). The Hindi prayer repeats verses 7–13 whole: Mahiṣa-crusher Mahālakṣmī, three-powered, born of all gods' bodies (7); white face, blue arms, snowy breasts, red waist and feet, blue thighs, pride-mad (8); bright robes-jewels-paints, beauty-luck-rich (9); eighteen arms for worship though thousand-armed in truth, weapons told low-right onward (10): beads 1, lotus 2, arrow 3, sword 4, thunderbolt 5 (with variants: mace 6, discus 7, trident 8, axe 9, conch 10, bell 11, noose 12) (11); spear 13, staff 14, shield 15, bow 16, cup 17, flask 18 — weapon-graced arms, lotus-seated (12); worship this all-gods-made, all-mighty Mahālakṣmī, O king, and rule all worlds and gods (13). One book reads 'worshipping' and 'of all worlds' here.

passages.mula:
गौरीदेहात्समुद्भूता या सत्त्वैकगुणाश्रया ।
साक्षात् सरस्वती प्रोक्ता शुम्भासुरनिबर्हिणी ॥१४॥
passages.primaryEn: From Gaurī's body rose She, resting on goodness alone — Sarasvatī Herself, killer of Śumbha-demons. (Verse 14.) In simple words the bright daughter's changed face: born from Fair Gaurī's body, pure goodness only — Sarasvatī in person, Śumbha's slayer.

passages.mula:
दधौ चाष्टभुजा बाणमुसले शूलचक्रभृत् ।
शवं घण्टां लाङ्गलं च कार्मुकं वसुधाधिप ॥१५॥
passages.primaryEn: Eight-armed She held arrow, club, spear, discus; corpse, bell, plough and bow too, O earth-lord. (Verse 15.) In simple words Her eight hands: arrow, club, spear, discus — plus corpse, bell, plough and bow.

passages.mula:
एषा सम्पूजिता भक्तया सर्वज्ञत्वं प्रयच्छति ।
निशुम्भमथनी देवी शुम्भासुरनिबर्हिणी ॥१६॥
passages.primaryEn: Worshipped with love She grants all-knowing — Niśumbha-pounder, Śumbha-demon-ender Goddess. (Verse 16.) In simple words: love-worshipped, She gives total wisdom — grinder of Niśumbha, finisher of Śumbha.

passages.mula:
इत्युक्तानि स्वरूपाणि मूर्तीनां तव पार्थिव ।
उपासनं जगन्मातुः पृथगासां निशामय ॥१७॥
passages.primaryEn: Thus are told the faces of the forms, O king; now hear, apart, the world-Mother's worship. (Verse 17.) In simple words the sage closes the face-list and opens the worship-manual: faces told — now learn how to serve each, one by one.

passages.mula:
महालक्ष्मीर्यदा पूज्या महाकाली सरस्वती ।
दक्षिणोत्तरयोः पूज्ये पृष्ठतो मिथुनत्रयम् ॥१८॥
passages.primaryEn: When four-armed Mahālakṣmī is worshipped, Mahākālī-Sarasvatī right-left; behind, the three pairs. (Verse 18.) Combined with the commentaries: now Mahālakṣmī's worship: right-left split follows the worshipper. And in Her changed form, worship-modes: 'eighteen-armed' — right-left follows the Goddess, since 'Her' is stressed; though ten-faced has two faces per ten arms, when the chief goddess is served in second form the other two serve as limbs in second form too — but served in first form, they serve in first form. 'Great Lakṣmī' lacks a second-case ending, since 'thus' already says the object-hood. When the other two are served freely, with no fixed must-do, He tells only their shared threefold rite in verse-and-half: 'eighteen-armed' — 'right-left' joins what follows. In the gods' three free separate rites too, south holds Time, north Death — both deities to serve, is the sense. (Verses 18–22.) The Hindi prayer repeats it whole: worship four-armed Mahālakṣmī centre, four-armed Mahākālī right, Mahāsarasvatī left, and the three pairs behind (18).

passages.mula:
विरिञ्चिः स्वरया मध्ये रुद्रो गौर्या च दक्षिणे ।
वामे लक्ष्म्या हृषीकेशः पुरतो देवतात्रयम् ॥१९॥
passages.primaryEn: Brahmā with Learning centre, Rudra with Gaurī right; with Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu left; before, the goddess-triad. (Verse 19.) In simple words the couple-seating: centre Brahmā-Learning, right Rudra-Gaurī, left Viṣṇu-Lakṣmī, and the three goddesses facing them in front.

passages.mula:
अष्टादशभुजा मध्ये वामे चास्या दशानना ।
दक्षिणेऽष्टभुजा लक्ष्मीर्महतीति समर्चयेत् ॥२०॥
passages.primaryEn: Eighteen-armed centre, ten-faced left of Her, eight-armed Lakṣmī right — worship thus the Great One. (Verse 20.) In simple words the second seating: centre eighteen-armed Mahālakṣmī, left ten-faced Mahākālī, right eight-armed Mahāsarasvatī — worship the Great Goddess so.

passages.mula:
अष्टादशभुजा चैषा यदा पूज्या नराधिप !।
दशानना चाष्टभुजा दक्षिणोत्तरयोस्तदा ॥२१॥
passages.primaryEn: And when the eighteen-armed is worshipped, O king of men — ten-faced and eight-armed right-left then. (Verse 21.) In simple words the free-standing rite: serve the eighteen-armed One alone, with ten-faced right and eight-armed left.

passages.mula:
कालमृत्यू च सम्पूज्यौ सर्वारिष्टप्रशान्तये ।
यदा चाष्टभुजा पूज्या शुम्भासुरनिबर्हिणी ॥२२॥
passages.primaryEn: Time and Death both to be served, for all evils' calming; and when eight-armed Śumbha-killer is worshipped. (Verse 22.) Combined with the commentaries: the three pairs are seated place-wise — 'Brahmā and the rest' (19). Right-left follows the Goddess in Her changed-form modes (20); the second-form rule for limbs; and in free separate rites, Time south, Death north (21–22). The Hindi prayer continues: behind centre-Mahālakṣmī — Brahmā-Learning centre, Rudra-Gaurī right, Viṣṇu-Lakṣmī left, three goddesses in front (19); centre eighteen-armed, left ten-faced, right eight-armed — so serve the Great One (20); served freely apart, right and left of them… (21; Time and Death next).

passages.mula:
भलीभाँति पूजा सभी प्रकार के अरिष्टों की शान्ति के लिये करनी चाहिये। जब
शुम्भ नामक असुर को मारने वाली अष्टभुजा की पृथक् पूजा करनी हो ॥ २२॥
passages.primaryEn: Time south and Death north serve well, to calm all evils; when the eight-armed Śumbha-killer is served apart. (Verse 22, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee notes the two guardian extras — Time and Death — who keep every misfortune quiet.

passages.mula:
नवास्याः शक्तयः पूज्यास्तथा रुद्रविनायकौ ।
नमो देव्या इति स्तोत्रैर्महालक्ष्मीं समर्चयेत् ॥२३॥
passages.primaryEn: Her nine powers be served, and Rudra-Vināyakas both; with 'salutation to Goddess' hymns, worship great Lakṣmī. (Verse 23.) In simple words: serve Her nine powers (Brāhmī and the eight sisters), Rudra right and Gaṇeśa left, chanting 'salutation to the Goddess' over great Lakṣmī.

passages.mula:
अवतारत्रयार्चायां स्तोत्रमन्त्रास्तदाश्रयाः ।
अष्टादशभुजा चैषा पूज्या महिषमर्दिनी ॥२४॥
passages.primaryEn: In the three descents' worship, hymn-mantras stay with their homes; and eighteen-armed Buffalo-killer is worshippable. (Verse 24.) In simple words the mantra-rule: each descent is hymned with its own hymns — Mahākālī with 'You are Svāhā, You are Svadhā', Mahālakṣmī with 'the Goddess by whom all this is spread', Mahāsarasvatī with 'O Goddess who rescues the surrendered in pain' — and chief over all for Caṇḍī-praisers, daily and on wish-days, stands eighteen-armed middle-story Mahālakṣmī; the other two, served-or-not as you will. Since She is the Whole, serving Her nearly serves the other two — hence He describes Her alone at length. (Continued next.)

passages.mula:
महालक्ष्मीर्महाकाली सैव प्रोक्ता सरस्वती ।
ईश्वरी पुण्यपापानां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरी ॥२५॥
passages.primaryEn: Mahālakṣmī, Mahākālī — She alone is called Sarasvatī; Queen of merit and sin, great Queen of all worlds. (Verse 25.) Combined with the Hindi: on Her right serve Rudra, on Her left Vināyaka Gaṇeśa, plus Her nine powers — Brāhmī 1, Māheśvarī 2, Kaumārī 3, Vaiṣṇavī 4, Vārāhī 5, Nārasiṃhī 6, Aindrī 7, Śivadūtī 8, Cāmuṇḍā 9 — chanting 'salutation to the Goddess' over four-armed Mahālakṣmī (23). For the three descents use their own hymn-mantras — eighteen-armed for 'the Goddess by whom', ten-faced for the night-hymn, eight-armed for the Nārāyaṇī-hymn; Buffalo-killer eighteen-armed Mahālakṣmī is the special worship (24). For She alone is hailed Mahālakṣmī, Mahākālī, Sarasvatī — Queen ruling merit and sin, great Queen of all the worlds. (25.)

passages.mula:
तत्पूजयैवान्ययोः पूजितप्रायत्वादिति ध्वननाय विस्तरेण तदेव वर्णयति ।
अष्टादशेत्यादिना।। २४॥२५॥
passages.primaryEn: She alone is Mahālakṣmī, Mahākālī, Sarasvatī — ruler of merit and sin, great Queen of all worlds. (Verse 25, Hindi seal.) In simple words the oneness is driven home: three names, one Queen — over every deed, every world.

passages.mula:
वे ही महालक्ष्मी, महाकाली और महासरस्वती कही गयीं हैं। वे ही पुण्य और
पाप की ईश्वरी (नियन्त्री) हैं और सम्पूर्ण लोकों की महेश्वरी हैं।। २५॥
passages.primaryEn: Who worshipped Buffalo-ender becomes world-lord; worship the world's nurse, Caṇḍikā, lover of devotees. (Verse 26.) In simple words the standing order: whoever served Mahiṣa-ender Lakṣmī has ruled worlds — so serve the world-nurse, devotee-loving Caṇḍikā.

passages.mula:
महिषान्तकरी येन पूजिता स जगत्प्रभुः ।
पूजयेज्जगतां धात्रीं चण्डिकां भक्तवत्सलाम् ॥२६॥
passages.primaryEn: With guest-gifts and the rest. (Verse 27, with an old quoted line.) Combined with the old note: 'with guest-gifts' — then offerings. In simple words the worship-ware list begins: welcome-water and the rest to follow.

passages.mula:
अर्ध्यादिभिरलङ्कारैर्गन्धपुष्यैस्तथाक्षतैः
धूपैदपैश्च
passages.primaryEn: With offerings of many eatables. (Verse 27, Hindi listing.) Combined with the old note: 'I' — then with many-eatables offerings. In simple words the food-offerings: many tasty dishes heaped before Her.

passages.mula:
रुधिराक्तेन बलिना मांसेन सुरया नृप ! ।
प्रणामाचमनीयेन चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना ॥२८॥
passages.primaryEn: With blood-wet victim, flesh and wine, O king; with bow-water, sandal sweet-smelling. (Verse 28.) In simple words the fierce offerings: blood-smeared victim, meat and wine; sipping-water and sweet sandal.

passages.mula:
सकर्पूरैश्च ताम्बूलैर्भक्तिभावसमन्वितैः ।
वामभागेऽग्रतो देव्याश्छिन्नशीर्ष महासुरम् ॥२९॥
passages.primaryEn: With camphor betels, full of loving devotion; to the Goddess's left-front, the beheaded great demon. (Verse 29.) In simple words: camphor-rolled betel-leaves offered with love — and to Her left-front, the beheaded mighty demon (Mahiṣa) himself is worshipped.

passages.mula:
पूजयेन्महिषं येन प्राप्तं सायुज्यमीशया ।
दक्षिणे पुरतः सिहं समग्रं धर्ममीश्वरम् ॥३०॥
passages.primaryEn: Worship the buffalo — by whom union with the Lady was won; to the right-front, the lion — all-dharma, the Lord. (Verse 30.) In simple words: worship the buffalo too, for through Her it won oneness with the Goddess; and to Her right-front, the lion — dharma itself in full, the Lord's own form.

passages.mula:
वाहनं पूजयेद्देव्या धृतं येन चराचरम् ।
यः कुर्यात् प्रयतो धीमांस्तस्या एकाग्रमानसः ॥३१॥
passages.primaryEn: The Goddess's vehicle worship — by whom the moving world is held; whoever does, striving, wise, one-pointed in mind toward Her. (Verse 31.) Combined with Guptavatī's ritual grammar: verses 26–27 need nothing; on 'blood-wet' — victim-rules by brāhmaṇa and the rest were told before, not to be re-thought. (Verses 28–29.) The lion's vehicle-form is told: 'all-dharma' means the rite-acts taught by all fourteen lores. (Verse 30.) 'Whoever does Her worship' joins with what went before — he should worship the lion. (Verse 31.) The Hindi prayer repeats it whole: whoever served buffalo-ending Mahālakṣmī has been world-lord and shall be — so serve world-nurse, devotee-loving Caṇḍikā (26). Then Sumedhas tells the worship-mode, O king — with welcome-water and the rest, ornaments, scents, flowers, unbroken rice, lamp-incense, and many-eatables food-gifts (27); with blood-wet victim, flesh, wine, bowing and sipping water, sweet sandal (28); with loving camphor-betels and the rest. To the Goddess's left-front, that great demon of severed head (29) — worship Mahiṣa, who won union with the Lady. To Her right-front the lion — all-dharma itself, Lord-natured (30). The Goddess's vehicle, by whom the moving world is held. Then the wise man, striving, one-pointed toward Her, should hymn Her. (31.)

passages.mula:
ततः कृताञ्जलिर्भूत्वा स्तुवीत चरितैरिमैः ।
एकेन वा मध्यमेन नैकेनेतरयोरिह ॥३२॥
passages.primaryEn: Then, folded hands become, praise with these stories — with one, or the middle; not with one of the other two here. (Verse 32, with verse 33 quoted.) Combined with the old note: 'but don't chant for story-fruit — chanting gaps wins a hole.' Then circling and bowing, folded hands on the crown. (Verse 33.) In simple words the praise-rule: palms joined, hymn Her with these stories — with all three, or with the middle one alone; never with just one of the other two. And never chant half a story for its fruit — a gapped chant earns a hole.

passages.mula:
क्षमापयेज्जगद्धात्रीं मुहुर्मुहुरतन्द्रितः ।
प्रतिश्लोकं च जुहुयात् पायसं तिलसर्पिषा ॥३४॥
passages.primaryEn: Beg pardon of the world-nurse again and again, untiring; verse by verse offer milk-rice with sesame-ghee. (Verse 34.) Combined with the commentaries: 'then' — after limb-god worship, praise with the fit three stories, or middle-story alone, or all four hymns — for where the earlier choice fails, the later choice stands settled. (Verses 32–33.) 'Verse by verse' marks one of the told mantra-shares; here some offer fire per verse of armour-trio and mystery-trio both — but in the armour share fire is unfit, another lore forbids it, as: 'in Caṇḍī-praise, one fire per verse is wished; with armour-hymn mantras make no fire there; from blindness, whoever fires per verse with armour-hymns — his body shall fall, he'll reach hell; the great demon Andhaka, set on Durgā-fire, fell by Mahādeva for armour-fire-born sin' — and more. (Verse 34.) The Hindi prayer repeats: palms joined, praise with these three stories — or the middle story alone, never one of the other two (32). Never do half a story — half-reading may win harm. Then circling and bowing, palms-to-crown pose (33). Untiring, beg the world-nurse pardon again and again for faults and slips; then with sesame-ghee milk-rice, chanting each verse-mantra, offer fire. (Verse 34, Hindi.)

passages.mula:
जुहुयात्स्तोत्रमन्त्रैर्वा चण्डिकायै शुभं हविः ।
नमोनमःपदैर्देवीं पूजयेत्सुसमाहितः ॥३५॥
passages.primaryEn: Offer fair fire to Caṇḍikā with hymn-mantras or else; with 'salutation, salutation' words worship the Goddess, well-composed. (Verse 35.) In simple words: fire into Her flame with hymn-mantras — or else; then settled and calm, worship the Goddess chanting Her name-mantras with 'salutation, salutation'.

passages.mula:
प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिः प्रह्लः प्रणम्यारोप्य चात्मनि ।
सुचिरं भावयेदीशां चण्डिकां तन्मयो भवेत् ॥३६॥
passages.primaryEn: Striving, palms joined, humble — bowing, lifting Her into the self — long contemplate the Lady, Caṇḍikā, becoming Her. (Verse 36.) In simple words: striving, hands joined, bowing low, place all-goddess Caṇḍikā inside the heart and sit with Her long — until you become Her.

passages.mula:
एवं यः पूजयेद्भक्तत्या प्रत्यहं परमेश्वरीम् ।
भुक्त्वा कामान् यथाकामं देवीसायुज्यमाप्नुयात् ॥३७॥
passages.primaryEn: Who thus worships with love the supreme Lady day by day — enjoying wished joys as wished, he wins the Goddess's union. (Verse 37.) In simple words the daily fruit: love-worship Her every day — enjoy every wished joy to the full, then win oneness with the Goddess.

passages.mula:
यो न पूजयते नित्यं चण्डिकां भक्तवत्सलाम् ।
भस्मीकृत्यास्य पुण्यानि निर्दहेत्परमेश्वरी ॥३८॥
passages.primaryEn: Who worships not daily Caṇḍikā, lover of devotees — burning his merits to ash, the supreme Lady burns. (Verse 38.) In simple words the warning: skip daily worship of devotee-loving Caṇḍikā, and the supreme Lady burns your merits to ash and ash.

passages.mula:
तस्मात् पूजय भूपाल ! सर्वलोकमहेश्वरीम् ।
यथोक्तेन विधानेन चण्डिकां सुखमाप्स्यसि ॥३९॥
passages.primaryEn: So worship, O king! the great Queen of all worlds — by the told rule, Caṇḍikā — and you shall win joy. (Verse 39.) In simple words the sage closes: so worship Her, O king, world-Queen Caṇḍikā, exactly as told — and joy is yours.

passages.mula: इति वैकृतिकरहस्यं समाप्तम्।
passages.primaryEn: Thus ends the Vaikṛta mystery. Combined with the closers: the other path is told for the less able — 'offer with hymn-mantras or else'; this fire-rite belongs to worship's limbs. (Verses 35–36.) Her wished-and-daily natures are told in turn by 'who thus' in two verses. (37–38.) 'So' concludes. (39.) Thus ends the Guptavatī on the Vaikṛta mystery. The Hindi prayer continues: or else fire fair offerings with hymn-mantras alone (some use all four praises, some use 'to Caṇḍikā salutation' alone for the fire-rite). After fire, calm-minded, worship great Lakṣmī again chanting Her name-mantras. (Verse 35, Hindi; continues: bowing, heart-lifting, oneness — next.)

passages.mula:
विधान करते हैं)। हवन के पश्चात् समाहित चित्त होकर महालक्ष्मी देवी के नामों
से अर्थात् नाममन्त्रों का उच्चारण करके पुनः उनकी पूजा करनी चाहिये ।।३५॥
passages.primaryEn: After fire, worship again with name-mantras, calm-minded. (Verse 35, Hindi.) In simple words: fire done — sit still, chant Her names, worship again.

passages.mula:
तत्पश्चात् यत्नपूर्वक अञ्जलि बाँधकर (हाथ जोड़कर), विनम्र होकर देवी को
प्रणाम कर, हृदय में उन सर्वेश्वरी चण्डिका का आरोप करके दीर्घकाल तक उनकी
passages.primaryEn: Then striving, palms joined, humble, bowing to the Goddess, lifting the all-Queen Caṇḍikā into the heart, contemplate long and grow into Her. (Verse 36, Hindi, with old note + variant.) Combined with the old note: whoever love-worships the supreme Lady daily enjoys wished joys and wins Goddess-union (37). Whoever worships not daily devotee-loving Caṇḍikā — his merits the supreme Lady burns to ash (38). So, O king, worship world-great-Queen Caṇḍikā by the told rule — and you shall win joy (39). One book reads 'again with name-words' and 'joys' here.

passages.mula:
नन्दा भगवती नाम या भविष्यति नन्दजा ।
सा स्तुता पूजिता भक्तत्या वशीकुर्याज्जगत्त्रयम् ॥१॥
passages.primaryEn: Blessed Nandā the Goddess, who shall be born of Nanda — praised and worshipped with love, She lays all three worlds at (the worshipper's) feet. (Mūrti verse 1.) In simple words the mystery of faces opens: the coming Goddess named Nandā, born of Nanda — love-serve Her and all three worlds come under your sway.

passages.mula:
कनकोत्तमकान्तिः सा सुकान्तिकनकाम्बरा ।
देवी कनकवर्णाभा कनकोत्तमभूषणा ॥२॥
passages.primaryEn: Of finest-gold glow, lovely-glow golden-robed Goddess — gold-hued, gloriously gold-decked. (Verse 2.) In simple words Nandā shines: finest gold Her glow, lovely gold Her robes, golden Her color, finest gold Her jewels.

passages.mula:
कमलाङ्कुशपाशाब्जैरलङ्कृतचतुर्भुजा 1
इन्दिरा कमला लक्ष्मीः सा श्रीरुक्माम्बुजासना ॥३॥
passages.primaryEn: Lotus, goad, noose, conch-graced, four-armed; Indirā, Kamalā, Lakṣmī — She, Fortune, lotus-golden-seated. (Verse 3.) In simple words Her four arms hold lotus, elephant-goad, noose and conch; and She is hailed Indirā, Kamalā, Lakṣmī, Fortune Herself, seated on a golden lotus.

passages.mula:
या रक्तदन्तिका नाम देवी प्रोक्ता मयाऽनघ ! ।
तस्याः स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि शृणु सर्वभयापहम् ॥४॥
passages.primaryEn: The Goddess named Raktadantikā, O sinless, told by me — Her form I shall tell; hear, remover of all fears. (Verse 4.) In simple words the sage turns to the next face: sinless king, I told you of blood-toothed Raktadantikā — now hear Her form, which ends every fear.

passages.mula:
रक्ताम्बरा रक्तवर्णा रक्तसर्वाङ्गभूषणा ।
रक्तायुधा रक्तनेत्रा रक्तकेशातिभीषणा ॥५॥
passages.primaryEn: Red-robed, red-hued, red-all-limbs-decked; red-weaponed, red-eyed, red-haired, most dread. (Verse 5.) In simple words She is red all over: red clothes, red color, red jewels on every limb, red weapons, red eyes, dread red hair.

passages.mula:
रक्ततीक्ष्णनखा रक्तदशना रक्तदन्तिका ।
पतिं नारीवानुरक्ता देवी भक्तं भजेज्जनम् ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: Red sharp nails, red teeth — Raktadantikā; as a loving wife loves her lord, the Goddess loves Her worshipping folk. (Verse 6.) Combined with Guptavatī's grammar: now the seven faces from Nandā are worshipped in brief. 'With lotus-goad-noose' — lotus means conch, or lotus itself, since elsewhere in Lakṣmī-focus two lotuses in two hands are seen. (Verses 1–5.) 'As a wife her lord' is a likeness only in the loving part. (Verse 6.) The Hindi prayer repeats it whole: Nandā, born of Nanda, love-served, lays three worlds at feet (1); finest-gold glow, lovely gold robes, gold-hued, finest-gold-decked (2); four arms graced with lotus, goad, noose, conch — hailed Indirā, Kamalā, Lakṣmī, Fortune, golden-lotus-seated (3); O sinless king, now hear blood-toothed Raktadantikā's form, ender of all fears (4); red-robed, red-hued, red-jewelled everywhere, red-weapons, red eyes, dread red hair (5); sharp red nails, red teeth — hence Raktadantikā. (Continues: loving as a wife loves — next.)

passages.mula:
वाली हैं। ऐसी यह देवी अपने भक्तजन को इस प्रकार मानती हैं जैसे कोई
अनुरक्त स्त्री अपने पति को माने ॥ ६॥
passages.primaryEn: As a loving wife loves her lord, so the Goddess loves Her devotees. (Verse 6, Hindi.) In simple words the tenderness is sealed: Her love for devotees is exactly a devoted wife's love for her husband — total and personal.

passages.mula:
वसुधेव विशाला सा सुमेरुयुगलस्तनी ।
दीर्घौ लम्बावतिस्थूलौ तावतीव मनोहरौ ॥७॥
passages.primaryEn: Vast as the earth, Her breasts twin Merus; long and hanging, over-plump, yet utterly charming. (Verse 7.) In simple words the cosmic-mother image: vast as earth, breasts like twin Meru peaks — long, hanging, full — and utterly lovely.

passages.mula:
कर्कशावतिकान्तौ तौ सर्वानन्दपयोनिधी ।
भक्तान् सम्पाययेद्देवी सर्वकामदुधौ स्तनौ ॥८॥
passages.primaryEn: Hard yet most lovely, twin seas of all bliss — the Goddess feeds devotees the wish-cow breasts. (Verse 8.) In simple words: firm yet beautiful, oceans of all joy — with those wish-fulfilling breasts the Mother nurses Her devotees.

passages.mula:
खड्गं पात्रं च मुशलं लाङ्गलं च बिभर्ति सा ।
आख्याता रक्तचामुण्डा देवी योगेश्वरीति च ॥९॥
passages.primaryEn: Sword and cup, club and plough She bears — hailed blood-Cāmuṇḍā, and Goddess queen of yogis. (Verse 9.) In simple words Her four hands: sword, wine-cup, club, plough — and She is hailed blood-Cāmuṇḍā, queen of all yogis.

passages.mula:
अनया व्याप्तमखिलं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
इमां यः पूजयेद्भक्त्या स व्याप्नोति चराचरम् ॥१०॥
passages.primaryEn: By Her is pervaded the whole still-moving world; whoever worships Her with love pervades the moving world. (Verse 10.) In simple words: She fills everything still and moving — and whoever loves Her fills the moving world too.

passages.mula:
अधीते य इमं नित्यं रक्तदन्त्या वपुःस्तवम् ।
तं सा परिचरेद्देवी पतिं प्रियमिवाङ्गना ॥११॥
passages.primaryEn: Whoever daily reads this body-praise of blood-toothed (Raktadantikā) — the Goddess serves him as a wife serves a dear lord. (Verse 11.) In simple words the daily-reader's reward: chant Her body-praise every day, and the Goddess Herself serves you as a wife serves her beloved.

passages.mula:
शाकम्भरी नीलवर्णा नीलोत्पलविलोचना ।
गम्भीरनाभिस्त्रिवलीविभूषिततनूदरी ॥१२॥
passages.primaryEn: Śākambharī blue-hued, blue-lotus-eyed; deep-navelled, triple-fold graced slim-bellied. (Verse 12.) In simple words the next face: blue-complexioned, blue-lotus-eyed, deep-navelled, slim-waisted with three lovely folds.

passages.mula:
सुकर्कशसमोत्तुङ्गवृत्तपीनघनस्तनी
मुष्टिं शिलीमुखापूर्ण कमलं कमलालया ॥१३॥
passages.primaryEn: Hard, matched, high, round, plump, full breasts; fist full of arrows, lotus — lotus-homed. (Verse 13.) Combined with the commentaries: verses 7–8 need nothing; 'cup' is the honey-drinking tool. (Verses 9–12.) 'Arrow-fists' — arrows: She bears bow-arrow-lotus-missiles in four hands, is the sense. (Verse 13.) The Hindi prayer repeats it whole: blood-toothed Goddess vast as earth, breasts twin Merus — long, hanging, over-plump, yet utterly charming (7); hard yet most lovely, seas of all bliss — with wish-cow breasts the Goddess feeds devotees (8); sword, cup, club, plough in four hands — hailed blood-Cāmuṇḍā, queen of yogis (9); by Her the whole still-moving world is pervaded; whoever loves Her pervades the moving world (10). (Continues: daily body-praise, Śākambharī's blue form — next.)

passages.mula:
हुए स्तनवाली हैं। कमल पर निवास करने वाली यह परमेश्वरी अपने हाथों में
बाणों से पूर्ण मुष्टि, कमल (धारण करती हैं ।। १३॥
passages.primaryEn: Daily body-praise wins Her wifely service; Śākambharī's blue lotus-eyes, deep navel, triple-fold slim waist. (Verses 11–12, Hindi.) Combined with the split notes: whoever daily reads this body-praise of blood-toothed Raktadantikā is served by the Goddess as a wife serves a dear lord (11); blue-hued Śākambharī, blue-lotus-eyed, deep-navelled, triple-fold graced slim-bellied (12). (Continues: hard matched breasts, arrow-fist, lotus — next.)

passages.mula:
पुष्पपल्लवमूलादिफलाढ्यं शाकसञ्चयम् ।
काम्यानन्तरसैर्युक्तं क्षुत्तृण्मृत्युज्वरापहम् ॥१४॥
passages.primaryEn: Flower, leaf, root and fruit-rich, a greens-heap — wished, endless-tasted — ending hunger, thirst, death, fever. (Verse 14.) In simple words Śākambharī the herb-bearer: heaps of greens — flowers, leaves, roots, fruits — of every wished taste, endless, curing hunger, thirst, death and fever.

passages.mula:
कार्मुकं च स्फुरत्कान्ति बिभ्रती परमेश्वरी ।
शाकम्भरी शताक्षी सा सैव दुर्गा प्रकीर्तिता ॥१५॥
passages.primaryEn: Bow of shooting light bearing, supreme Lady — Śākambharī, hundred-eyed, She alone is famed Durgā. (Verse 15.) In simple words: bow of flashing light in hand — and know: hundred-eyed Śākambharī is Herself famed Durgā, by time-place-state names.

passages.mula:
विशोका दुष्टदमनी शमनी दुरितापदाम् ।
उमा गौरी सती चण्डी कालिका सापि पार्वती ॥१६॥
passages.primaryEn: Sorrowless, wicked-tamer, calmer of sins and dangers — Umā, Gaurī, Satī, Caṇḍī, Kālikā too is Pārvatī. (Verse 16.) In simple words one garland of names: grief-free, punisher of the wicked, soother of sin and peril — Umā, Fair One, True One, Fierce One, Dark One — and all are Pārvatī.

passages.mula:
शाकम्भरीं स्तुवन् ध्यायञ्जपन् सम्पूजयन्नमन् ।
अक्षय्यमश्नुते शीघ्रमन्नपानामृतं फलम् ॥१७॥
passages.primaryEn: Praising, picturing, chanting, worshipping, bowing Śākambharī — soon wins food-drink-deathless fruit, unending. (Verse 17.) In simple words the all-in-one promise: hymn Her, picture Her, chant Her, serve Her, bow to Her — and soon win food, drink and deathless fruit that never ends.

passages.mula:
भीमापि नीलवर्णा सा दंष्ट्रादशनभासुरा ।
विशाललोचना नारी वृत्तपीनपयोधरा ॥१८॥
passages.primaryEn: Terrible too, blue-hued — fang-tooth shining; wide-eyed woman, round full-breasted. (Verse 18.) In simple words the seventh face, Bhīmā: blue-bodied even in terror, fangs and teeth agleam, wide eyes, woman's form, round full breasts.

passages.mula:
चन्द्रहासं च डमरु शिरःपात्रं च बिभ्रती ।
एकवीरा कालरात्रिः सैवोक्ता कामदा स्तुता ॥१९॥
passages.primaryEn: Moon-laugh (sword), drum, head-cup bearing — the One Heroine, Night-of-death, hailed wish-giver when praised. (Verse 19.) In simple words Her four hands: bright sword, little drum, skull-cup — hailed One Heroine and death-night, and praised, She grants every wish.

passages.mula:
तेजोमण्डलदुर्धर्षा भ्रामरी चित्रकान्तिभृत् ।
चित्रानुलेपना देवी चित्राभरणभूषिता ॥२०॥
passages.primaryEn: Hard to face through glory-orbed, bee-variegated, bright-hued; paint-pasted Goddess, bright-jewel-decked. (Verse 20.) Combined with the notes: the seventh face is told — 'glory' (verse 20). 'Moon-laugh' is the sword. (Verse 19.) On such spots only simile's shared ground is wanted, not full likeness — so the sage's point is just love's fullness. One book reads 'fear-remover' here. The Hindi prayer continues: greens-heaps of flower-leaf-root-fruit, endless-tasted, hunger-thirst-death-fever-ending (14); flashing bow in hand — the same Lady by time-place-state is Śākambharī, hundred-eyed, famed Durgā (15); sorrowless, wicked-taming, sin-peril-soothing — Umā, Gaurī, Satī (meant: Satī), Caṇḍikā, Kālikā and Pārvatī are all She (16); whoever hymns, pictures, chants, serves and bows Śākambharī soon wins food, drink and deathless unending fruit (17). (Continued: terrible blue Bhīmā — next.)

passages.mula:
जप, पूजा और नमस्कार करने वाला व्यक्ति शीघ्र ही अन्न, पान और अमृतफल
को प्राप्त करता है, जो अक्षय अर्थात् कभी नष्ट नहीं होता।।१७।।
passages.primaryEn: Whoever hymns, pictures, chants, serves and bows Her soon wins unending food-drink-deathless fruit. (Verse 17, Hindi.) In simple words: five-fold devotion — sing, see, chant, serve, bow — and deathless nourishment, forever, soon.

passages.mula:
वह भीमादेवी भी नीलवर्ण वाली ही हैं। दंष्ट्रा और दशन से प्रकाशित
हैं। विशाल नेत्रों वाली, स्त्री रूप वाली तथा गोल एवं पुष्ट पयोधर वाली
passages.primaryEn: Terrible blue Bhīmā, fang-tooth agleam, wide-eyed woman, round full-breasted. (Verse 18, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: in four hands — moon-laugh, drum, head and wine-cup bearing. (Continues: One Heroine, death-night, wish-giver when praised — next.)

passages.mula:
करती हैं। वे ही एकवीरा और कालरात्रि नामवाली हैं। वे ही स्तुत अर्थात् पूजित
होने पर कामदा अर्थात् मनोरथ पूर्ण करने वाली हैं।।१९॥
passages.primaryEn: Moon-laugh, drum, head and cup in four hands — the One Heroine, death-night, wish-giver when praised. (Verse 19, Hindi.) In simple words: sword, drum, skull, cup — hail the lone heroine of death-night, and She fulfils every wish.

passages.mula: वह देवी भ्रामरी कही जाती हैं, जो विचित्र (अनेक रंग की) कान्ति को
passages.primaryEn: Bee-called Goddess, marvel-bright, glory-orbed unfaceable, many-painted, marvel-jewel-decked. (Verse 20, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: unfaceable through glory-orb, many body-paints, marvel-jewel-decked. (Verse 20.) In simple words: Bhrāmarī — shimmering many-hued, too bright to gaze at, painted and jewelled all over.

passages.mula:
चित्रभ्रमरपाणिः सा महामारीति गीयते ।
इत्येता मूर्तयो देव्या व्याख्याता वसुधाधिप ! ॥२१॥
passages.primaryEn: Wondrous-bee-handed, hailed great-plague — thus are told the Goddess's faces, O earth-lord! (Verse 21.) In simple words the face-list closes: marvel-bee in hand, hailed even as the great plague (that ends all plagues) — O king, so are the Goddess's faces told.

passages.mula:
जगन्मातुश्चण्डिकायाः कीर्तिताः कामधेनवः ।
इदं रहस्यं परमं न वाच्यं कस्यचित्त्वया ॥२२॥
passages.primaryEn: World-Mother Caṇḍikā's, when hailed — wish-cows; this top secret by you to none be told. (Verse 22.) In simple words: these faces of world-Mother Caṇḍikā, when hymned, are wish-cows granting every desire — but this topmost secret must never be told by you to anyone.

passages.mula:
व्याख्यानं दिव्यमूर्तीनामधीवाऽवहितः स्वयम् ।
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन देवीं जप निरन्तरम् ॥२३॥
passages.primaryEn: The god-faces' tale, read yourself, heedful; so with all effort chant the Goddess ceaselessly. (Verse 23.) In simple words the standing order: read this tale of divine faces yourself, carefully — and with every effort, chant the Goddess without a break.

passages.mula:
सप्तजन्मार्जितैघरह्महत्यासमैरपि
Π
पाठमात्रेण मन्त्राणां मुच्यते सर्वकिल्विषैः ॥२४॥
passages.primaryEn: By mere reading of mantras, from all sins — even seven-lives-gathered, priest-killing-like — one is freed. (Verse 24.) In simple words: just reading these mantras washes every sin — even priest-murder-grade sins piled over seven lifetimes.

passages.mula:
देव्या ध्यानं मया ख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं महत् ।
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥२५॥
passages.primaryEn: The Goddess's focus, told by me — secret of secrets, great; so with all effort, giver of every wished fruit. (Verse 25.) In simple words: this focus of the Goddess I have told — most secret of secrets, and giver of every wished fruit — strive for it with all your strength.

passages.mula: इति मूर्तिरहस्यं समाप्तम्।
passages.primaryEn: Thus ends the Mūrti mystery. Combined with the closers: verses 21–22 need nothing; and the study of all three mysteries too is ordained — 'the tale' — heedful means sense-heedful, and all is blessed. (Verses 23–25.) One book reads 'wish-fruit-giver' here. Thus ends the Guptavatī on the Mūrti mystery. (Running page dust follows.) In simple words the book seals itself: study all three mysteries with heedful sense — all blessed.

passages.mula:
चतुष्टये पीठिकानां प्राचीनानां च तुष्टये ।
चमत्कृतिकरी भूयान्नवीनानां च मत्कृतिः ॥१॥
passages.primaryEn: For the four ancient seat-lines' joy, and to amaze the new — may my work stand. (Colophon verse 1.) In simple words the author's closing prayer for his own book: may it delight the old traditions and astonish the new.

passages.mula:
साधुच्छाया प्रमितप्रमोदवर्षे चिदम्बरे जनिता ।
साधुच्छायाप्रमितप्रमोदवर्षं चिदम्बरे तनुतात् ॥२॥
passages.primaryEn: Born in holy-shade, measured-joy-year, in mind-sky — may it spread holy-shade, measured-joy-year in mind-sky. (Colophon verse 2, chronogram.) In simple words a blessing in riddle-words hiding the work's birth-year: may it spread holy shade and measured joy in the sky of minds.

passages.mula:
गुरुरेव शिवो गुरुमेव भजे गुरुणैव सहास्मि नमो गुरवे ।
न गुरोरधिकं शिशुरस्मि गुरोर्मतिरस्तु गुरौ जयनाथगुरौ ॥३॥
passages.primaryEn: The teacher alone is Śiva — the teacher alone I serve; with the teacher alone I stand — salutation to the teacher. Naught is higher than the teacher — I am the teacher's child; may mind rest in the teacher, in victorious master-teacher. (Colophon verse 3.) In simple words the author's vow: teacher is Śiva, teacher is refuge, teacher is company — I am the teacher's child, salutation to the teacher.

passages.mula:
श्रीकाशीपुरवासिसोमपसुधीगम्भीरराभारती-
पुत्रेणाग्निचिता मया रचितया चण्डीस्तुतेष्टीकया ।
या नन्दादिषु सप्तमी भ्रमरिणी भीमातटे सन्नति-
क्षेत्रे नः कुलदेवता वसति सा श्रीचन्द्रला प्रीयताम् ॥४॥
passages.primaryEn: By me — son of deep-voiced Bhāratī, Soma-drinking thinker of Kāśī-city, thrice-fire-piled — made as this Caṇḍī-praise brick-sacrifice: She who among Nandā and the rest is seventh, bee-faced, on terror's bank in our family-goddess field dwelling — may holy Candralā be pleased. (Colophon verse 4.) In simple words Bhāskararāya signs his work: a Kāśī scholar, thrice fire-sacrificer, built this commentary as a brick-altar of praise; and may our family Goddess — seventh among Nandā and the rest, bee-faced, dwelling by the terror-river in our holy field — holy Candralā, be pleased.

passages.mula:
इति श्रीमत्पदवाक्यप्रमाणपारावारीणधुरीणसर्वतन्त्र-
स्वतन्त्रश्रीमद्‌गम्भीरराय भारतीदीक्षितात्मज भास्कर राय भारती-
दीक्षितमहाग्निचिता विरचिता गुप्तवतीसमाख्या सप्तशतीव्याख्या समाप्ता ।
नमश्चण्डिकायै नमो नमः
न वै देयमनुक्रोशाद्दीनार्तातुरकेष्वपि ।
आप्ताचरित इत्येव धर्म इत्येव वा पुनः ॥१॥
passages.primaryEn: Thus ends the Guptavatī-named Saptashatī explanation, composed by thrice-fire-piled Bhāskararāya Bhāratī-Dīkṣita, son of all-Tantra-free master Gambhīrarāya Bhāratī-Dīkṣita, crown-jewel among word-proof-and-reason ocean-crossers. Salutation to Caṇḍikā, salutation salutation. 'Not to be given — from pity even to the poor-suffering-sick; deemed as saints' conduct, or else as duty.' (Verse 1, colophon seal.) In simple words the book closes with its author's full signature and one last guard-rule: this teaching is not to be handed out — not even from pity to the poor, sick or suffering — unless as saints' conduct, or else as duty.

passages.mula:
अपराधसहस्राणि क्रियन्तेऽहर्निशं मया ।
दासोऽयमिति मां मत्वा क्षमस्व परमेश्वरि ! ॥१॥
passages.primaryEn: Thousands of faults I do day and night; knowing 'this is my servant', forgive me, supreme Lady! (Pardon verse 1.) In simple words the poet's daily confession begins: day and night I pile up thousands of faults — but I am Your servant; knowing just that, forgive me, Mother Supreme.

passages.mula:
आवाहनं न जानामि न जानामि विसर्जनम् ।
पूजां चैव न जानामि क्षम्यतां परमेश्वरि ! ॥२॥
passages.primaryEn: I know not inviting, nor know I bidding farewell; nor know I worship's way — forgive, supreme Lady! (Pardon verse 2.) In simple words: I don't know how to call You, how to send You off, how to worship at all — forgive me anyway.

passages.mula:
मन्त्रहीनं क्रियाहीनं भक्तिहीनं सुरेश्वरि !
यत्पूजितं मया देवि ! परिपूर्णं तदस्तु मे ॥३॥
passages.primaryEn: Mantra-less, rite-less, love-less, O queen of gods — whatever worship I did, O Goddess, let it stand full for me. (Pardon verse 3.) In simple words: my worship lacked mantra, lacked rite, lacked love — yet let it count as full, by Your grace making up every lack.

passages.mula:
अपराधशतं कृत्वा जगदम्बेति चोच्चरेत् ।
यां गतिं समवाप्नोति न तां ब्रह्मादयः सुराः ॥४॥
passages.primaryEn: Having done a hundred faults, crying 'O Mother of the world!' — the goal he wins, not even Brahmā and the gods. (Pardon verse 4.) In simple words the wonder-promise: commit a hundred faults, then just cry 'Mother of the world!' — and win a goal even Brahmā and the gods cannot reach.

passages.mula:
सापराधोऽस्मि शरणं प्राप्तस्त्वां जगदम्बिके ! ।
इदानीमनुकम्प्योऽहं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥५॥
passages.primaryEn: Faulty I am, sheltered in You, O Mother of the world; now I deserve mercy — do with me as You will. (Pardon verse 5.) In simple words total surrender: guilty, yes — but sheltered in You; now I am Yours to mercy; do whatever You wish with me.

passages.mula:
अज्ञानाद्विस्मृतेर्भ्रान्त्या यन्यूनमधिकं कृतम् ।
तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देवि ! प्रसीद परमेश्वरि ! ॥६॥
passages.primaryEn: Whatever was done less or more, unknowing, forgetting, erring — all of it forgive, O Goddess; be pleased, supreme Lady! (Pardon verse 6, Hindi.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: day and night I commit thousands of faults — knowing 'he is my servant', forgive them graciously (1); I know no inviting, no farewell, no worship-way — forgive (2); O Goddess, queen of gods, my mantra-less, rite-less, love-less worship — let it stand full by Your grace (3); doing a hundred faults yet crying 'Mother of the world' wins a goal beyond even Brahmā and the gods (4); O Mother of the world, I am faulty but sheltered in You — now deserving mercy, do as You will (5).

passages.mula:
हे देवि ! परमेश्वरि ! आज्ञान से, भूल से अथवा भ्रान्ति से मैंने जो न्यूनता या
अधिकता कर दी हो, वह सब क्षमा करो और प्रसन्न होओ ॥ ६॥
passages.primaryEn: O Goddess, supreme Lady — whatever lack or excess I did unknowing, forgetting, erring — forgive it all and be pleased. (Verse 6, Hindi.) In simple words the last word: unknowing, forgetting, mistaking — however I fell short or overdid — forgive everything, and smile on me.

passages.mula:
780 दुर्गासप्तशती
कामेश्वरि ! जगन्मातः ! सच्चिदानन्दविग्रहे ! ।
गृहाणार्चामिमां प्रीत्या प्रसीद परमेश्वरि ! ॥७॥
